payload.author: andrewtdiz
payload.body:
## Summary

Perry currently accepts `wrap` and `wrapper` as named ESM exports from `node:module` / `module`, but Node rejects those names at module instantiation time.

The local manifest marks both entries as module exports:

```rust
// crates/perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs
property("module", "wrap"),
property("module", "wrapper"),
```

That creates a false-positive compatibility surface: users can write code that type/checks and runs under Perry, but cannot load under Node.

## Reproduction

```ts
import { wrap, wrapper } from "node:module";

console.log("wrap:", typeof wrap);
console.log("wrapper:", Array.isArray(wrapper), typeof wrapper);
```

## Node baseline

On Node v25.9.0:

```text
file:///private/tmp/perry-node-compat-main/tmp-module-wrap-export-probe.ts:1
import { wrap, wrapper } from "node:module";
         ^^^^
SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:module' does not provide an export named 'wrap'
```

## Perry behavior

On Perry `22824ba90` / `perry 0.5.1055`:

```text
$ target/release/perry check tmp-module-wrap-export-probe.ts
Checking 1 file(s)...

All checks passed! - 1 file(s) checked
```

```text
$ target/release/perry run tmp-module-wrap-export-probe.ts
wrap: undefined
wrapper: false undefined
```

## Expected behavior

- `import { wrap, wrapper } from "node:module"` should be rejected like Node rejects it.
- `perry --print-api-manifest` should not report `wrap` or `wrapper` as top-level ESM exports for `module` / `node:module`.
- The existing namespace behavior, `import * as Module from "node:module"; Module.wrap`, can still read as `undefined`.
- If Perry later supports the CommonJS `Module` constructor/default object shape, expose these helpers there in coordination with #3713 rather than as ESM named exports.

## Existing coverage gap

`test-parity/node-suite/module/imports/wrap-wrapper-undefined.ts` covers namespace reads:

```ts
import * as Module from "node:module";
console.log(typeof Module.wrap);
console.log(typeof Module.wrapper);
```

That is not enough to catch this issue because Node allows absent namespace properties to read as `undefined`, but rejects absent named exports during ESM linking. A focused Node API parity regression should assert that the named import fails before execution.

No Test262 work is required for this gap.
payload.title: node:module: wrap and wrapper are accepted as ESM named exports but Node rejects them

## Summary

Under the normal non-interactive parity harness, Node allows `new tty.WriteStream(1)` and `new tty.WriteStream(2)` even when stdout/stderr are pipes rather than TTYs. Perry throws `SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED` for those same constructors.

This is separate from optional real-PTY coverage (#1271). The mismatch is observable in CI-safe, non-interactive execution and blocks using the exported `WriteStream` constructor for stdout/stderr fds in the same way Node permits.

Baseline: `22824ba90abf Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)`.

## Probe

```ts
import tty from "node:tty";

function check(label: string, fn: () => unknown) {
  try {
    const value = fn();
    console.log(label + ":", value);
  } catch (err: any) {
    console.log(label + " THROW:", err?.name, err?.code || "no-code", err?.message || "");
  }
}

check("WriteStream fd1 fd", () => new tty.WriteStream(1).fd);
check("WriteStream fd2 fd", () => new tty.WriteStream(2).fd);
check("ReadStream fd0 fd", () => new tty.ReadStream(0).fd);
check("WriteStream invalid -1", () => new tty.WriteStream(-1).fd);
check("ReadStream invalid -1", () => new tty.ReadStream(-1).fd);
```

## Node behavior

Node v25.9.0 under this non-interactive harness:

```text
WriteStream fd1 fd: undefined
WriteStream fd2 fd: undefined
ReadStream fd0 fd THROW: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED TTY initialization failed: uv_tty_init returned EINVAL (invalid argument)
WriteStream invalid -1 THROW: RangeError ERR_INVALID_FD "fd" must be a positive integer: -1
ReadStream invalid -1 THROW: RangeError ERR_INVALID_FD "fd" must be a positive integer: -1
```

Node distinguishes the write side from the read side for standard pipe fds: read stream construction fails for fd 0, while write stream construction for fd 1/2 succeeds.

## Perry behavior

`target/release/perry check tmp-tty-fd-probe.ts`:

```text
All checks passed! - 1 file(s) checked
```

`target/release/perry run tmp-tty-fd-probe.ts`:

```text
WriteStream fd1 fd THROW: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED TTY initialization failed
WriteStream fd2 fd THROW: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED TTY initialization failed
ReadStream fd0 fd THROW: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED TTY initialization failed
WriteStream invalid -1 THROW: RangeError ERR_INVALID_FD "fd" must be a positive integer: -1
ReadStream invalid -1 THROW: RangeError ERR_INVALID_FD "fd" must be a positive integer: -1
```

Invalid fd validation already matches the broad Node shape; the issue is the valid stdout/stderr write-fd constructor path.

## Existing local context

- `docs/runtime-parity-gaps.md` currently lists `readStream.fd` and `writeStream.fd` as the remaining `node:tty` gaps.
- #1271 tracks optional PTY-backed tests for real interactive terminal behavior.
- #3906 tracks default import shape for `node:tty` and other builtins.

This issue should stay focused on CI-safe constructor behavior for non-TTY stdout/stderr fds.

## Acceptance

- `new tty.WriteStream(1)` and `new tty.WriteStream(2)` no longer throw under the non-interactive parity harness.
- The observed `fd` property and basic shape match Node for stdout/stderr pipe fds.
- `new tty.ReadStream(0)` continues to throw `ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED` when stdin is not a TTY, matching Node in this harness.
- Negative fd validation continues to throw `RangeError ERR_INVALID_FD`.
- Add or update a deterministic `node-suite/tty` fixture for the fd 1/2 constructor behavior; keep real PTY behavior in #1271.

No Test262 scope; this is Node API compatibility.
payload.title: node:tty: WriteStream(1/2) throws under non-TTY stdout/stderr where Node constructs

payload.author: andrewtdiz
payload.body:
## Summary

Perry accepts default imports for several CommonJS-backed Node builtins, but the runtime default value is not the Node-compatible module object for some modules. In the current probe, `node:tty`, `node:v8`, `node:http2`, `node:perf_hooks`, and `node:util/types` default imports produce placeholder-looking objects whose enumerable keys are only `__module__`, and `node:timers/promises` default import produces a boolean.

Node exposes a real default object for these builtins. Code using `import mod from "node:<builtin>"` can therefore pass Perry `check` but observe a different runtime shape.

Baseline: `22824ba90abf Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)`.

There is a focused issue for `node:child_process` default import shape (#3706). This issue tracks the broader default-export behavior across other builtins.

## Probe

```ts
import tty from "node:tty";
import fs from "node:fs";
import buffer from "node:buffer";
import v8 from "node:v8";
import http2 from "node:http2";
import perfHooks from "node:perf_hooks";
import utilTypes from "node:util/types";
import timersPromises from "node:timers/promises";

for (const [name, value] of [
  ["tty", tty],
  ["fs", fs],
  ["buffer", buffer],
  ["v8", v8],
  ["http2", http2],
  ["perf_hooks", perfHooks],
  ["util/types", utilTypes],
  ["timers/promises", timersPromises],
] as const) {
  console.log(name, typeof value, value && typeof value === "object" ? Object.keys(value).slice(0, 3).join(",") : "");
}
```

## Node behavior

Node v25.9.0:

```text
tty object isatty,ReadStream,WriteStream
fs object appendFile,appendFileSync,access
buffer object Buffer,transcode,isUtf8
v8 object cachedDataVersionTag,getHeapSnapshot,getHeapStatistics
http2 object connect,constants,createServer
perf_hooks object Performance,PerformanceEntry,PerformanceMark
util/types object isArgumentsObject,isArrayBuffer,isAsyncFunction
timers/promises object setTimeout,setImmediate,setInterval
```

## Perry behavior

`target/release/perry check tmp-default-import-tail-probe.ts`:

```text
All checks passed! - 1 file(s) checked
```

`target/release/perry run tmp-default-import-tail-probe.ts`:

```text
tty object __module__
fs object appendFile,appendFileSync,access
buffer object Buffer,transcode,isUtf8
v8 object __module__
http2 object __module__
perf_hooks object __module__
util/types object __module__
timers/promises boolean
```

`fs` and `buffer` look close in this sample; the mismatch is visible in the other listed builtins.

## Manifest/namespace context

A manifest-vs-Node namespace audit shows many builtins where Node exposes `default` but Perry's manifest does not list it as a module export, including:

```text
buffer
dgram
dns
dns/promises
fs
https
http
http2
module
net
perf_hooks
process
readline
readline/promises
stream/promises
string_decoder
timers
timers/promises
tty
util/types
v8
worker_threads
zlib
```

Some of those default imports may already work, as `fs`/`buffer` do in the probe. The important gap is that Perry's default-import lowering/runtime path is inconsistent and can produce non-Node placeholder values.

## Expected

- For CommonJS-backed Node builtins, `import mod from "node:<builtin>"` should produce the same observable object shape as Node's default export.
- `namespace.default` and default import should agree for the covered modules.
- Default objects should expose the same public module members as the corresponding Node namespace/CommonJS export, not a placeholder `__module__` object or unrelated primitive.
- `perry --print-api-manifest`, generated docs, and DTS should represent supported default exports consistently.
- Add parity fixtures for a representative set such as `tty`, `v8`, `http2`, `perf_hooks`, `util/types`, and `timers/promises`.

No Test262 scope; this is Node API compatibility.

## Summary

Perry's current `node:http2` manifest exposes `createSecureServer`, the settings helpers, `constants`, and request/response classes, but it omits several public Node exports that define the non-secure server, client-session, upgrade-handshake, and sensitive-header symbol surface.

This means ordinary named imports that work in Node fail Perry `check` before runtime.

Baseline: `22824ba90abf Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)`.

## Current manifest gap

`target/release/perry --print-api-manifest` currently reports these `node:http2` module exports:

```text
createSecureServer
getDefaultSettings
getPackedSettings
getUnpackedSettings
Http2ServerRequest
Http2ServerResponse
constants
```

Node v25.9.0 also exposes:

```text
connect
createServer
performServerHandshake
sensitiveHeaders
default
```

There is an existing focused issue for `createSecureServer({})` warning during construction (#3884). This issue tracks the missing public export surface outside that constructor-specific behavior.

## Probe

```ts
import {
  connect,
  createServer,
  performServerHandshake,
  sensitiveHeaders,
} from "node:http2";

console.log("connect", typeof connect);
console.log("createServer", typeof createServer);
console.log("performServerHandshake", typeof performServerHandshake);
console.log("sensitiveHeaders", typeof sensitiveHeaders, String(sensitiveHeaders));
```

## Node behavior

Node v25.9.0:

```text
connect function
createServer function
performServerHandshake function
sensitiveHeaders symbol Symbol(sensitiveHeaders)
```

## Perry behavior

`target/release/perry check tmp-http2-export-probe.ts`:

```text
Checking 1 file(s)...
error[U006]: The requested module 'node:http2' does not provide an export named 'connect'
  --> /private/tmp/perry-node-compat-main/tmp-http2-export-probe.ts:2:4
  |
2 |   connect,
  |    ^^^^^^^

Check failed: 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)
Error: Check failed with errors
```

## Suggested scope

- Add/track `http2.connect(authority[, options][, listener])` and the `ClientHttp2Session`/stream surface needed for a minimal local client-server parity test.
- Add/track `http2.createServer([options][, onRequestHandler])` for non-TLS HTTP/2 server construction.
- Add/track `http2.performServerHandshake(socket[, options])` at least enough to expose the named API with intentional unsupported behavior if full handshake support is deferred.
- Add/track `http2.sensitiveHeaders` as the public symbol export.
- Align namespace/default export shape with Node for this module.

## Acceptance

- Named ESM imports for `connect`, `createServer`, `performServerHandshake`, and `sensitiveHeaders` pass Perry `check`.
- Namespace presence and `typeof` output match Node for the covered names.
- `sensitiveHeaders` is a stable symbol whose stringification matches Node's observable shape.
- A minimal `createServer`/`connect` loopback parity fixture either works end to end or is split into a follow-up with an explicit unsupported runtime error shape.
- Generated manifest/docs/DTS include the supported public exports.

No Test262 scope; this is Node API compatibility.

## Summary

Perry's current `node:v8` manifest omits several named exports that Node exposes in the ESM namespace. Code that imports modern V8 diagnostics/profiling helpers works in Node but fails Perry `check` before runtime.

Baseline: `22824ba90abf Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)`.

This complements the existing focused issues for heap snapshot output (#3140), startup snapshots (#3141), and promise hooks (#3139). This issue is specifically about the missing public named exports and parity coverage for the remaining modern helper surface.

## Current manifest gap

`target/release/perry --print-api-manifest` reports these `node:v8` module exports today:

```text
serialize
deserialize
getHeapStatistics
getHeapCodeStatistics
getHeapSpaceStatistics
cachedDataVersionTag
GCProfiler
Serializer
DefaultSerializer
Deserializer
DefaultDeserializer
startupSnapshot
promiseHooks
setFlagsFromString
takeCoverage
stopCoverage
setHeapSnapshotNearHeapLimit
```

Node v25.9.0 exposes additional named exports:

```text
getCppHeapStatistics
getHeapSnapshot
isStringOneByteRepresentation
queryObjects
startCpuProfile
writeHeapSnapshot
default
```

`getHeapSnapshot` and `writeHeapSnapshot` overlap with #3140. The other helpers are not covered by the existing `node:v8` issues found during triage.

## Probe

```ts
import {
  getCppHeapStatistics,
  getHeapSnapshot,
  isStringOneByteRepresentation,
  queryObjects,
  startCpuProfile,
  writeHeapSnapshot,
} from "node:v8";

for (const [name, value] of [
  ["getCppHeapStatistics", getCppHeapStatistics],
  ["getHeapSnapshot", getHeapSnapshot],
  ["isStringOneByteRepresentation", isStringOneByteRepresentation],
  ["queryObjects", queryObjects],
  ["startCpuProfile", startCpuProfile],
  ["writeHeapSnapshot", writeHeapSnapshot],
] as const) {
  console.log(name, typeof value);
}
```

## Node behavior

Node v25.9.0:

```text
getCppHeapStatistics function
getHeapSnapshot function
isStringOneByteRepresentation function
queryObjects function
startCpuProfile function
writeHeapSnapshot function
```

## Perry behavior

`target/release/perry check tmp-v8-modern-export-probe.ts`:

```text
Checking 1 file(s)...
error[U006]: The requested module 'node:v8' does not provide an export named 'getCppHeapStatistics'
  --> /private/tmp/perry-node-compat-main/tmp-v8-modern-export-probe.ts:2:4
  |
2 |   getCppHeapStatistics,

Check failed: 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)
  |    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Error: Check failed with errors
```

## Suggested scope

- Add/track `getCppHeapStatistics()`.
- Add/track `isStringOneByteRepresentation(value)`.
- Add/track `queryObjects(constructor[, options])`.
- Add/track `startCpuProfile([title])`.
- Ensure the heap snapshot named exports are included in the manifest/export shape as part of #3140 or this cut.
- Add Node-vs-Perry parity fixtures that at minimum prove these names are importable and function-valued.

## Acceptance

- Perry accepts named ESM imports for Node's current `node:v8` helper tail listed above.
- Namespace shape matches Node for the covered names, including `typeof` and basic presence checks.
- For helpers implemented as stubs initially, the thrown error shape is intentionally tracked and does not masquerade as a missing export.
- `getHeapSnapshot` / `writeHeapSnapshot` export-shape work is coordinated with #3140 so the public names and runtime contracts converge together.
- Generated manifest/docs/DTS include the same supported public `node:v8` exports.

No Test262 scope; this is Node API compatibility.

payload.body:
## Summary

On macOS, Node's `node:constants` ESM namespace does not export several Linux-only constants, but Perry's manifest/checker accepts them as named imports and Perry runs the program with each binding set to `undefined`.

This creates a false-positive Node API surface: code that fails during Node ESM instantiation passes Perry `check` and runs under Perry.

Baseline: `22824ba90abf Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)`.

## Claimed Perry surface

`target/release/perry --print-api-manifest` reports these as `node:constants` module exports on this macOS checkout:

```text
O_DIRECT
O_NOATIME
RTLD_DEEPBIND
SIGPOLL
SIGPWR
SIGSTKFLT
```

A manifest-vs-Node namespace audit shows these six names as Perry-only extras for `node:constants`:

```text
constants: claimed 237, Node namespace 231
extras: O_DIRECT, O_NOATIME, RTLD_DEEPBIND, SIGPOLL, SIGPWR, SIGSTKFLT
```

## Probe

```ts
import { O_DIRECT, O_NOATIME, RTLD_DEEPBIND, SIGPOLL, SIGPWR, SIGSTKFLT } from "node:constants";

console.log(O_DIRECT, O_NOATIME, RTLD_DEEPBIND, SIGPOLL, SIGPWR, SIGSTKFLT);
```

## Node behavior

Node v25.9.0 on this macOS machine rejects the import during ESM instantiation:

```text
SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:constants' does not provide an export named 'O_DIRECT'
```

Namespace reads also confirm these names are absent:

```text
O_DIRECT false undefined
O_NOATIME false undefined
RTLD_DEEPBIND false undefined
SIGPOLL false undefined
SIGPWR false undefined
SIGSTKFLT false undefined
```

## Perry behavior

`target/release/perry check tmp-constants-platform-named-import-probe.ts`:

```text
All checks passed! - 1 file(s) checked
```

`target/release/perry run tmp-constants-platform-named-import-probe.ts`:

```text
undefined undefined undefined undefined undefined undefined
```

Namespace reads match Node because they report absent/undefined:

```text
O_DIRECT false undefined
O_NOATIME false undefined
RTLD_DEEPBIND false undefined
SIGPOLL false undefined
SIGPWR false undefined
SIGSTKFLT false undefined
```

The mismatch is specifically the named-import/export surface.

## Expected

- On macOS/Darwin targets, Perry should not advertise or accept named ESM imports for `O_DIRECT`, `O_NOATIME`, `RTLD_DEEPBIND`, `SIGPOLL`, `SIGPWR`, or `SIGSTKFLT` from `node:constants`.
- Named imports of unavailable platform constants should fail the same way Node fails.
- Namespace reads of absent constants should continue to return `undefined`, matching current Node/Perry behavior.
- `perry --print-api-manifest` and generated docs/DTS should either be target-platform-sensitive for `node:constants` or clearly avoid claiming unavailable constants as module exports.

No Test262 scope; this is Node API compatibility.

payload.author: andrewtdiz
payload.body:
## Summary

`node:string_decoder` currently exposes `StringDecoder`, and Perry's checker accepts code that constructs it, but the runtime object does not behave like Node's `StringDecoder` instance. In Node, instances expose `write()` and `end()` on `StringDecoder.prototype`; in Perry, `new StringDecoder("utf8")` produces an object without those callable methods, so ordinary decoder usage fails at runtime.

There is a related manifest-shape cleanup: `perry --print-api-manifest` lists `encoding`, `lastChar`, `lastNeed`, and `lastTotal` as top-level `node:string_decoder` properties. Node does not export those names from the module namespace; they are instance/prototype/internal state. Perry already rejects named imports of those fields, matching Node, but the manifest/docs/DTS surface is misleading.

Baseline: `22824ba90abf Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)`.

## Node behavior

Probe:

```ts
import { StringDecoder } from "node:string_decoder";

const dec = new StringDecoder("utf8");
const proto = Object.getPrototypeOf(dec);

console.log("ctor:", typeof StringDecoder, StringDecoder.name);
console.log("instance ctor:", dec?.constructor?.name);
console.log("own keys:", Object.keys(dec).join(","));
console.log("proto keys:", Object.getOwnPropertyNames(proto).join(","));
console.log("typeof write:", typeof dec.write);
console.log("typeof end:", typeof dec.end);
console.log("write result:", dec.write(Buffer.from([0xE2, 0x82])));
console.log("end result:", dec.end(Buffer.from([0xAC])));
```

Node v25.9.0:

```text
ctor: function StringDecoder
instance ctor: StringDecoder
own keys: encoding
proto keys: constructor,write,end,text,lastChar,lastNeed,lastTotal
typeof write: function
typeof end: function
write result:
end result: €
```

## Perry behavior

`target/release/perry check tmp-string-decoder-instance-probe.ts`:

```text
All checks passed! - 1 file(s) checked
```

`target/release/perry run tmp-string-decoder-instance-probe.ts`:

```text
ctor: function StringDecoder
instance ctor: undefined
own keys:
TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at <anonymous>
```

A smaller direct-use probe also shows the user-facing failure:

```ts
import * as stringDecoder from "node:string_decoder";

console.log("namespace fields:", stringDecoder.encoding, stringDecoder.lastChar, stringDecoder.lastNeed, stringDecoder.lastTotal);
const dec = new stringDecoder.StringDecoder("utf8");
console.log("instance write:", dec.write(Buffer.from("ok")));
```

Node:

```text
namespace fields: undefined undefined undefined undefined
instance write: ok
```

Perry:

```text
namespace fields: undefined undefined undefined undefined
TypeError: write is not a function
    at <anonymous>
```

## Export-shape evidence

Node's module namespace has `StringDecoder` and `default`; it does not have top-level `encoding`, `lastChar`, `lastNeed`, or `lastTotal` exports. Both Node and Perry reject named imports like:

```ts
import { encoding } from "node:string_decoder";
```

But Perry's manifest currently reports these as module properties:

```text
StringDecoder class
encoding property
lastChar property
lastNeed property
lastTotal property
write/end instance methods
```

## Expected

- `new StringDecoder("utf8")` returns an instance whose prototype exposes Node-compatible `write()` and `end()` methods.
- Split multibyte decoding works like Node: incomplete bytes passed to `write()` are buffered and completed by `end()`.
- `Object.getPrototypeOf(new StringDecoder("utf8"))` is `StringDecoder.prototype`, with the expected prototype methods/state helpers.
- `perry --print-api-manifest` and generated docs/DTS stop claiming `encoding`, `lastChar`, `lastNeed`, and `lastTotal` as top-level module exports.
- Named imports of the non-exported fields remain rejected, and namespace reads of absent fields keep returning `undefined`, matching Node.

No Test262 scope here; this is Node API compatibility.
payload.title: node:string_decoder: StringDecoder instances are missing write/end behavior

payload.author: andrewtdiz
payload.body:
## Summary

Perry's `node:worker_threads` manifest/runtime currently models `workerData` as both a value export and a callable method, and also lists a non-Node `getWorkerData()` top-level method. Node exposes `workerData` as a value export only; there is no `getWorkerData` export, and `worker_threads.workerData()` throws because the value is not callable.

This is a narrow API-shape compatibility gap. The main-thread `workerData` value itself is already tracked/fixed separately in #3395; this issue is about removing/reclassifying the non-Node callable surface and making calls match Node's TypeError behavior.

## Current-main evidence

Baseline:

```text
22824ba90abf Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)
```

Manifest rows from `target/release/perry --print-api-manifest` include both a method and property for `workerData`, plus a `getWorkerData` method:

```text
worker_threads getWorkerData {"kind":"Method","has_receiver":false,"class_filter":null}
worker_threads workerData    {"kind":"Method","has_receiver":false,"class_filter":null}
worker_threads workerData    {"kind":"Property"}
```

Source search shows the same extra callable routing:

```text
crates/perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs:2487 getWorkerData
crates/perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs:2495 workerData
crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/native_table/extras.rs:98  method: "getWorkerData"
crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/native_table/extras.rs:107 method: "workerData"
```

Node v25.9.0 namespace shape:

```console
$ node --input-type=module -e 'const ns = await import("node:worker_threads"); for (const name of ["workerData","getWorkerData"]) console.log(name, Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ns,name), name in ns, typeof ns[name]);'
workerData true true object
getWorkerData false false undefined
```

Node rejects the named import for `getWorkerData`:

```console
$ node --input-type=module --eval "import { getWorkerData, workerData } from 'node:worker_threads'; console.log(typeof getWorkerData, workerData);"
SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:worker_threads' does not provide an export named 'getWorkerData'
```

Perry also rejects that named import despite the manifest row:

```console
$ target/release/perry check tmp-worker-getworkerdata-probe.ts
error[U006]: The requested module 'node:worker_threads' does not provide an export named 'getWorkerData'
```

But Perry does accept and run the non-Node callable `workerData()` path:

```ts
import * as workerThreads from "node:worker_threads";

try {
  const value = (workerThreads as any).workerData();
  console.log("workerData call:", value);
} catch (e: any) {
  console.log("workerData call error:", e.name, e.code ?? "");
}
console.log("workerData value:", workerThreads.workerData);
```

Node output:

```text
workerData call error: TypeError
workerData value: null
```

Perry output:

```text
workerData call: undefined
workerData value: null
```

So the value export is now correct on the main thread, but the callable shape is not Node-compatible.

## Scope

- Remove or reclassify `getWorkerData` from the public `node:worker_threads` manifest/docs/type surface.
- Remove or reclassify the top-level method form of `workerData`; keep `workerData` as a property/value export.
- Ensure `worker_threads.workerData()` follows normal JS semantics and throws `TypeError` because the value is not callable.
- Keep the current correct main-thread `workerData === null` behavior and related value exports from #3395.
- Keep `getEnvironmentData()` / `setEnvironmentData()` behavior unchanged; those are real Node exports.

## Acceptance

## Summary

Perry's strict built-in API gate currently rejects some namespace property reads that Node treats as ordinary JavaScript property misses returning `undefined`.

This surfaced in the curated DNS constants fixture on current `origin/main@22824ba90abf`: `node:dns/promises` intentionally does **not** export `ADDRCONFIG`, `V4MAPPED`, or `ALL`, but reading those properties from the namespace object is valid in Node and returns `undefined`. Perry rejects the property read at check/lower time before the runtime can produce the matching value.

This is separate from named ESM import validation. Node rejects `import { ADDRCONFIG } from "node:dns/promises"`, and Perry should continue not claiming that named export. The compatibility gap is namespace/property-read semantics.

## Local evidence

Current main:

```text
22824ba90abf Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)
```

Node v25.9.0 behavior for the namespace object:

```console
$ node -e 'import("node:dns/promises").then(m=>{for (const k of ["ADDRCONFIG","V4MAPPED","ALL","NODATA","CANCELLED"]){console.log(k, Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(m,k), k in m, typeof m[k], m[k]);}})'
ADDRCONFIG false false undefined undefined
V4MAPPED false false undefined undefined
ALL false false undefined undefined
NODATA true true string ENODATA
CANCELLED true true string ECANCELLED
```

Node rejects the corresponding named import, which is correct and should remain true:

```console
$ node --input-type=module -e 'import { ADDRCONFIG } from "node:dns/promises"; console.log(ADDRCONFIG)'
SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:dns/promises' does not provide an export named 'ADDRCONFIG'
```

Perry currently rejects the namespace property read in the curated fixture:

```console
$ target/release/perry check test-parity/node-suite/dns/constants/error-aliases.ts
error[U006]: `dns/promises.ADDRCONFIG` is not implemented in Perry — see `perry --print-api-manifest` for the supported surface, or set `PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1` to ignore. (#463)
  --> test-parity/node-suite/dns/constants/error-aliases.ts:9:48
```

The manifest matches Node for named exports: `dns/promises` includes DNS error aliases like `NODATA` and `CANCELLED`, but does not include `ADDRCONFIG`, `V4MAPPED`, or `ALL`.

With the gate bypassed, Perry's runtime output matches Node for this fixture, including the absent namespace properties:

```console
$ PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1 target/release/perry run test-parity/node-suite/dns/constants/error-aliases.ts
...
dnsPromises.ADDRCONFIG: undefined
dnsPromises.V4MAPPED: undefined
dnsPromises.ALL: undefined
...
named aliases: ENODATA ECANCELLED
```

The relevant gate is in `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_member.rs`: namespace `PropertyGet` on a `NativeModuleRef(module)` fails whenever `module_has_symbol(module, prop)` is `None`, even when the Node-compatible value for a namespace property miss is simply `undefined`.

## Scope

Make Node built-in namespace property reads distinguishable from named imports/calls:

- `import * as dnsPromises from "node:dns/promises"; dnsPromises.ADDRCONFIG` should compile and evaluate to `undefined`, matching Node.
- Similar absent-property reads on strict native module namespaces should follow normal JS property semantics when the code is only reading the value.
- Named imports for absent exports should remain rejected, matching Node's ESM behavior.
- Obvious unsupported API calls should still get the helpful Perry unimplemented-API error; this issue should not silently allow `fs.notARealMethod()`-style call gaps unless the runtime has a deliberate JS-compatible fallback.

## Acceptance

- `target/release/perry check test-parity/node-suite/dns/constants/error-aliases.ts` passes without `PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1`.
- The DNS constants fixture prints the same shape as Node for:
  - absent `dns/promises.ADDRCONFIG`, `V4MAPPED`, and `ALL` namespace reads (`undefined`), and
  - present DNS error aliases (`NODATA`, `CANCELLED`, etc.).
- A named import probe

## Summary

The curated `node:http` suite is mostly green on current main, including Agent hooks, IncomingMessage behavior, server headers/body, trailers, aliases, default connection headers, and timeout knobs. The remaining deterministic failure is the HTTP upgrade/WebSocket path: Perry delivers the same echoed text frame twice, while Node delivers it once.

This is not the `http.WebSocket` export-shape issue (#2566). The failing fixture exercises `http.Server`'s `upgrade` event and raw socket/WebSocket upgrade pumping semantics.

No Test262 coverage is involved; this is Node API compatibility evidence only.

## Local evidence

Baseline:

```text
22824ba90 Expose globalThis.EventTarget (#3628)
```

Command:

```bash
./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module http
```

```text
server-message: hello
client-frame: echo:hello
```

The fixture performs a deterministic raw HTTP upgrade handshake, sends one masked client text frame (`hello`), and expects one server echo frame (`echo:hello`). Perry correctly reaches the upgrade handler and logs the server message once, but the client observes the echo frame twice.

- Whether both raw-socket and WebSocket pump paths are active for the same frame.
- Whether the server-side `send`/`write` path replays buffered upgrade data after already delivering it.

`node:constants` mostly matches Node for the covered flat constants, but the ESM namespace shape is wrong: Perry claims a `constants.default` manifest entry, and default import / `process.getBuiltinModule("constants")` work, but `import * as constantsNs from "node:constants"` does not expose the `default` key that Node exposes.


```bash
target/release/perry --print-api-manifest > /tmp/perry-api-manifest.json
jq -r '.entries[] | select(.module=="constants") | .name' /tmp/perry-api-manifest.json | sort | rg '^default$|F_OK|R_OK|SIGHUP'
```

Perry claims `default` plus the flat constants:

```text
F_OK
R_OK
SIGHUP
default
```

Parity command:

```bash
./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module constants
```

Report:

```text
/private/tmp/perry-node-compat-main/test-parity/reports/parity_report_20260531_151601.json
```

Summary:

```text
Parity Pass:   3
Parity Fail:   1
```

```text
namespace default identity: true
builtin default identity: true
```

```diff
 https agent methods: function function function function function function
 https agent override: true
 https request overload: POST https: 127.0.0.1 /a?b=1 1
-https get overload: POST https: 127.0.0.1 /get?b=2 1
-https server methods: function function function
-https server knobs: 123 234 345 456 789 9
-https server setTimeout: true 567
+TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON
+    at <anonymous>
```

Fixture line:

```ts
const getReq = https.get(
  new URL("https://127.0.0.1:1/get?b=2"),
  { method: "POST", timeout: 1 },
  () => {},
);
```

Node returns a request object with:

```text
method: POST
protocol: https:
host: 127.0.0.1
path: /get?b=2
```

The relevant overload plumbing is in `crates/perry-codegen/src/lower_call/native_table/http.rs`, which routes `https.get` to `js_https_get_overload` with `NA_VARARGS`.

- `parse_request_overload(...)`
- `build_request_from_overload(...)`
- `request_parts_from_options(primary, options, "https", force_get)`
- `url_from_js_value(primary, default_protocol)`

The failure shape suggests the URL object is falling through to a JSON/stringification path for object URL extraction rather than reading the URL `href`/path fields in a Node-compatible way.

## Acceptance

- `https.get(new URL("https://127.0.0.1:1/get?b=2"), { method: "POST", timeout: 1 }, cb)` returns a request handle instead of throwing.

- Preserve the already-green parts of the fixture: `globalAgent`, `Agent` properties/methods/override, and `https.request(url, options, cb)` overload behavior.

## Summary

The curated `node:fs` parity suite is now broadly green on the last buildable main baseline, but two argument-validation fixtures still diverge from Node in error-message details. This is a focused child of the broader validation theme in #2013.

This matters because Perry now implements most of the filesystem surface semantically; the remaining compatibility gap is no longer "fs missing", it is Node-compatible `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` message/argument attribution on specific overloads.

## Current evidence

Baseline: `aed3a2b1b985` (`chore: complete stream tasklist reconciliation (#3790)`). Current `origin/main` is still build-red from #3864, so this used the last buildable main baseline.

Command run sequentially:

```sh
./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module fs
```

Result:

```text
Parity Pass:   158
Parity Fail:   2
Compile Fail:  0
Parity Rate:   98.7%
```

Failing fixtures:

```text
node-suite/fs/callbacks/arg-validation
node-suite/fs/sync/arg-validation-details
```

### Callback overload tail

Fixture line: `test-parity/node-suite/fs/callbacks/arg-validation.ts` calls:

```ts
fs.symlink("/tmp/perry_callback_arg_validation_a", "/tmp/perry_callback_arg_validation_b", "file")
```

Observed diff:

```diff
 symlink type missing cb name TypeError
 symlink type missing cb code ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
-symlink type missing cb message The "cb" argument must be of type function. Received type string ('file')
+symlink type missing cb message The "cb" argument must be of type function. Received undefined
```

Node treats the third argument as the callback in this overload shape; Perry treats it as `type` and then reports the missing callback as `undefined`.

### `copyFileSync` mode validation tail

Fixture line: `test-parity/node-suite/fs/sync/arg-validation-details.ts` calls:

```ts
fs.copyFileSync("/tmp/perry_sync_arg_validation_missing_a", "/tmp/perry_sync_arg_validation_missing_b", "x" as any)
```

Observed diff:

```diff

-sync copy mode string message mode must be int32 or null/undefined
+sync copy mode string message The "mode" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('x')
```

Node uses its short `mode must be int32 or null/undefined` message for this path; Perry currently uses the generic numeric argument message.

## Acceptance

- `./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module fs` passes sequentially.
- The fix preserves the already-green fs surface: callbacks, fd operations, glob, imports, mkdtempDisposable, openAsBlob, pathlikes, readdir/opendir, stats/statfs, streams, sync mutators, UTF8Stream, and watch fixtures.
- The behavior is coordinated with #2013, but scoped to the two current `node-suite/fs` tails rather than the older broad validation backlog.

This is a focused follow-up to closed #2962: the CBC finalized-handle cases now match, but several GCM-specific cases still do not.

## Current evidence

Baseline: `aed3a2b1b985` (`chore: complete stream tasklist reconciliation (#3790)`). Current `origin/main` is build-red from #3864, so I used this last buildable baseline.

Command run sequentially:

```sh
./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module crypto
```

Suite result:

```text
Parity Pass:   201
Parity Fail:   1
Compile Fail:  5
Parity Rate:   99.5%
```

Runtime mismatch:

```diff
-gcm-cipher-methods: function undefined
+gcm-cipher-methods: function function
 gcm-get-auth-tag-before-final err Error ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_STATE Invalid state for operation getAuthTag
 gcm-set-aad-after-update err Error ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_STATE Invalid state for operation setAAD
-gcm-final ok buffer:0
+gcm-final ok buffer:3
 gcm-get-auth-tag-after-final ok buffer:16
-gcm-decipher-methods: undefined function
-decipher-final-no-tag err Error  Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data
+gcm-decipher-methods: function function
+decipher-final-no-tag ok undefined
 decipher-set-auth-tag-after-final err Error ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_STATE Invalid state for operation setAuthTag
 decipher-set-auth-tag-first ok object
-decipher-set-auth-tag-second err Error ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_STATE Invalid state for operation setAuthTag
+decipher-set-auth-tag-second ok object
```

Fixture: `test-parity/node-suite/crypto/cipher/invalid-state-errors.ts`.

## Expected Node behavior

For AES-GCM handles:

- Encrypt-side `Cipheriv` exposes `getAuthTag`, but not `setAuthTag`.
- Decrypt-side `Decipheriv` exposes `setAuthTag`, but not `getAuthTag`.
- `cipher.final()` after `cipher.update("abc")` returns an empty Buffer because the ciphertext was emitted by `update()`.
- `decipher.final()` without an auth tag throws `Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data`.
- A second `decipher.setAuthTag(...)` throws `ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_STATE`.

## Perry source pointers

Local source inspection points at `crates/perry-stdlib/src/crypto/cipher.rs`:

- `dispatch_cipher_property()` currently returns bound closures for both `getAuthTag` and `setAuthTag` on every `CipherHandle`, so method exposure is not operation-specific.
- `dispatch_cipher()` has a `setAuthTag` finished guard, but the duplicate-tag case is still accepted because `state.auth_tag = Some(tag)` overwrites the first tag.
- GCM decrypt without a tag currently falls through to `nanbox_undefined()` instead of throwing the Node auth failure.
- The encrypted output distribution still differs for this fixture: Node emits the GCM ciphertext from `update()` and an empty Buffer from `final()`, while Perry emits bytes at `final()`.

## Acceptance

- `node-suite/crypto/cipher/invalid-state-errors` passes sequentially.
- Existing AES-CBC/ECB/GCM roundtrip fixtures remain green.
- The fix stays scoped to the handle-backed `createCipheriv` / `createDecipheriv` API, not stream-backed crypto transform parity (#2479).

## Summary

The curated `node:events` suite currently stalls before runtime on the EventEmitter `captureRejections` fixture. This blocks verification of a Node behavior that packages rely on: when an async listener rejects under `{ captureRejections: true }`, the rejection should be routed to the emitter's `error` event.

Current `origin/main` is build-red at `d4f2903fa567` (#3864), so this was verified on the previous buildable main:

```text
target/release/perry test-parity/node-suite/events/emitter/capture-rejections.ts -o /tmp/perry_parity_node-suite__events__emitter__capture-rejections
```

Fixture:

```ts
import { EventEmitter } from "node:events";

const ee = new EventEmitter({ captureRejections: true });
const events: string[] = [];
ee.on("x", async () => { throw new Error("async bad"); });
ee.on("error", (err: any) => events.push("error:" + err.message));
```

## Summary

`JSON.stringify` of a **boxed primitive wrapper** (`new String(x)` / `new Number(x)`
/ `new Boolean(x)`) returns `{}` instead of serializing via the wrapped primitive
value. Per spec, `JSON.stringify` calls the wrapper's internal `[[StringData]]` /
`[[NumberData]]` / `[[BooleanData]]` (via `toJSON`/coercion), so a `String` wrapper
serializes as the JSON string, a `Number` wrapper as the number, etc.

## Reproduction

```ts
console.log(JSON.stringify(new String("T")));   // Perry: {}   Node: "T"
console.log(JSON.stringify(new Number(42)));     // Perry: {}   Node: 42
console.log(JSON.stringify(new Boolean(true)));  // Perry: {}   Node: true

// Also surfaces via a primitive `this` (sloppy-mode boxing), e.g.
function f(this: any) { return this; }
console.log(JSON.stringify(f.apply("T", [])));   // Perry: [... {} ...]  Node: "T"
```

`typeof` already agrees (`"object"` for the wrapper in both), so the boxing itself
is correct — only the `JSON.stringify` serialization path doesn't unwrap.

A primitive `this` value passed to `Function.prototype.apply`/`call` is boxed to such
a wrapper (sloppy mode), so this is the residual difference in the #3828 minimal
repros that use a string thisArg (`f.apply("T", [1,2])`). It is independent of
call/apply/bind dispatch — it reproduces with `new String("T")` directly.

## Notes

Found while fixing #3828 (PR #3856). The call/apply/bind dispatch itself is correct;
this is purely the JSON serializer not unwrapping boxed primitive wrapper objects.
payload.title: JSON.stringify of boxed primitive wrappers (new String/Number/Boolean) returns {} instead of the primitive

## Summary

`Function.prototype.call` / `.apply` / `.bind` do **not** work as first-class inherited methods on function **values**. Perry handles the *static, directly-written* shapes (`Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments)`, `fn.apply(thisArg, [literal])`) via compile-time AST rewrites, but a function **value flowing through a variable** — especially the builtin function-method values `Function.prototype.call`/`apply`/`bind` themselves — has no working path, as either a value read or a dynamic dispatch.

This is the central blocker for the entire intrinsics/call-binding utility layer (`function-bind`, `call-bind-apply-helpers`, `call-bound`, `hasown`, `get-intrinsic`), which sits under a huge fraction of npm — including Express (#3527).

## Minimal reproductions

```ts
function f(this: any, a: any, b: any) { return [this, a, b]; }

// (1) `.call` / `.apply` read as a VALUE on a function
typeof (f as any).apply   // Perry: "undefined"   Node: "function"
typeof (f as any).call    // Perry: "undefined"   Node: "function"

// (2) direct .apply on a user-function value with a literal array — WORKS today
(f as any).apply("T", [1, 2])           // Perry: ["T",1,2]  ✅

// (3) builtin function-method value held in a var, then .apply on it
const c: any = Function.prototype.call;
typeof c.apply                          // Perry: "undefined"   Node: "function"
c.apply(f, ["X", 9, 8])                 // Perry: undefined     Node: ["X",9,8]
```

### Real-world failure chain (how Express hits it)

`hasown/index.js`:
```js
var call = Function.prototype.call;
var $hasOwn = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty;
var bind = require('function-bind');     // plain-closure bind
module.exports = bind.call(call, $hasOwn);   // → should be hasOwn(o, p)
```
`bind.call(call, $hasOwn)` returns a closure whose body does
`target.apply(that, args.concat(...))`, where `target === Function.prototype.call`.
That inner `target.apply(...)` throws **`TypeError: apply is not a function`**
(captured function-method value, dynamic args). So `hasown`'s export ends up
non-callable, and the first consumer — `get-intrinsic`'s
`hasOwn(INTRINSICS, name)` — throws `TypeError: value is not a function` at
module init, aborting the whole program.

Standalone repro of the hasown pattern:
```ts
function bind(this: any, that: any) {
  var target = this;
  var args = Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments, 1);
  return function (this: any) {
    return target.apply(that, args.concat(Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments)));
  };
}
var call = Function.prototype.call;
var $hasOwn = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty;
var hasOwn: any = (bind as any).call(call, $hasOwn);
var o: any = { a: 1 };
hasOwn(o, "a");  // Node: true ; Perry: throws "apply is not a function"
```

## Root cause

- The existing handling, `try_builtin_prototype_method_apply_call`
  (`crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call/intrinsics.rs`), is a **compile-time
  AST rewrite**. It only fires when:
  - the receiver is a statically recognizable `X.prototype.method` /
    array/string literal (`is_builtin_prototype_receiver`), **and**
  - the `.apply` args are a **literal array** (statically expandable).
  It rewrites `Recv.method.call(thisArg, a, b)` → `(thisArg).method(a, b)`.
- It cannot handle a function **value** in a variable, a **captured** function,
  or **non-literal** args (`args.concat(...)`) — exactly the function-bind /
  call-bind / hasown shapes.
- `.call` / `.apply` / `.bind` read as plain **values** (not immediately
  invoked) resolve to `undefined` (`typeof` is `"undefined"`), so feature
  detection and the `Function.prototype.call.bind(...)` idiom break.

## What already exists (so this is wiring, not a new engine)

- `js_closure_call_array(closure, args_array)` — invoke a closure with args
  pulled from an array (this *is* `.apply` semantics).
- `js_function_bind(...)` — bind support.

The runtime primitives are present; what's missing is the **method-dispatch
wiring** that routes `.call` / `.apply` / `.bind` on
payload.title: Function.prototype.call/apply/bind don't work on function values (dynamic dispatch + value reads) — blocks function-bind/call-bind/hasown/get-intrinsic (#3527)

Perry currently has contradictory `node:wasi` signals: the parity skiplist says WASI is out of scope for native AOT compilation, but `origin/main` still advertises a `wasi` module surface in the API manifest and generated docs. There is no dedicated open `node:wasi` issue; the only broad runtime-control umbrella I found was #3601, which is closed.

## Current local evidence

Environment:

- Node probe: `node:v25.9.0`
- Perry manifest source: `origin/main@bf4b4d2f4`, `crates/perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs`
- Local Perry manifest command on this branch: Perry `0.5.1044`, 2062 entries / 95 modules

Node's ESM namespace for `node:wasi` is small:

```text

=> WASI, default
```

Perry's manifest source advertises a richer WASI surface:

```rust
class("wasi", "WASI"),
method("wasi", "WASI", false, None),
method("wasi", "getImportObject", true, Some("WASI")),
method("wasi", "start", true, Some("WASI")),
method("wasi", "initialize", true, Some("WASI")),
method("wasi", "finalizeBindings", true, Some("WASI")),
property("wasi", "wasiImport"),
```

But `scripts/parity-skiplist.toml` explicitly excludes the module:

```toml
"wasi" = "WASI sandbox runtime; orthogonal to native AOT compilation."
```

## Why this matters

The manifest is part of Perry's API compatibility contract and feeds check/type/doc behavior. If `node:wasi` is intentionally unsupported, the manifest should not make it look supported. If Perry wants package feature detection to pass, the module needs a deliberate Node-compatible shape and error behavior instead of accidental metadata.

This is separate from #3804's general ESM named-export hygiene: #3804 can fix receiver methods leaking as top-level imports, but `node:wasi` also needs a module-level support decision.

## Scope

- Decide whether `node:wasi` is supported, explicitly unsupported, or supported only as feature-detection stubs.
- If unsupported, remove or reclassify `wasi` manifest entries and make `perry check` / generated docs report the module as skipped or unsupported consistently.
- If supported as a shape stub, expose `WASI` and `default.WASI` in CommonJS/ESM-compatible form and make unsupported operations fail with deterministic Node-shaped errors.

## Summary

Node still exposes a set of deprecated but observable legacy core modules such as `_http_agent`, `_http_client`, `_http_common`, `_http_incoming`, `_http_outgoing`, `_http_server`, `_stream_*`, `_tls_common`, and `_tls_wrap`. Perry currently neither claims them in the API manifest nor skiplists them as intentionally unsupported, so they sit outside the normal Node compatibility radar.

This is a phase-2 legacy-module cut, separate from the closed #3603 work. #3603 covered `node:sqlite`, `domain`, `punycode`, `sys`, `constants`, and `trace_events`; it did not classify the underscore compatibility modules that Node's builtin table still exposes.

- Perry manifest source checked from `origin/main` at `fc59040f8`
- Skiplist: `scripts/parity-skiplist.toml` does not skip the underscore modules.

- #3760, #3761, #3762, and #3784 cover current public transport/timer modules, not these deprecated alias modules.

Add deterministic node-suite coverage or an equivalent t

## Summary

Modern Node compatibility includes Web-compatible globals, not only `node:*` modules. Perry still has open, package-visible gaps across Fetch constructors/body APIs, FormData, DOM Event/EventTarget, WebSocket, worker messaging globals, WebCrypto globals, and Performance constructors. This epic groups those global-constructor and global-namespace cuts into one implementer-sized phase-2 issue after the closed #3598 umbrella.

## Local evidence

- `docs/runtime-parity.md` catalogs Node Web/global APIs, including `fetch`, `Headers`, `Request`, `Response`, `Blob`, `File`, `FormData`, streams, DOM events, `MessageChannel`, `MessagePort`, `BroadcastChannel`, `WebSocket`, WebCrypto, and Performance globals.
- `docs/runtime-parity-gaps.md` still identifies Web / Global APIs as a large true-gap bucket and warns that FFI/manifest existence is not semantic compatibility.
- Curated coverage exists under `test-parity/node-suite/globals`, `test-parity/node-suite/fetch`, `test-parity/node-suite/buffer/blob-file`, `test-parity/node-suite/crypto/webcrypto`, `test-parity/node-suite/perf_hooks`, and `test-parity/node-suite/worker_threads`.
- `scripts/parity-skiplist.toml` does not skip this Web/global surface.
- The previous umbrella #3598 is closed, but the child leaves below remain open and current.

## Related existing issues

- #2583 / #2924 - expose `fetch` as a first-class `globalThis` function
- #2608 - bind `Blob`, `Headers`, `Request`, and `Response` globals to real classes
- #2606 - implement `FormData` constructor and methods
- #2620 - implement `Request.formData()` and `Response.formData()`
- #2622 - implement `Request.blob()` and `Request.clone()`
- #2637 - align `Response.redirect()` validation and statusText
- #2597 - expose `MessageChannel`, `MessagePort`, and `BroadcastChannel` globals
- #2662 - expose `WebSocket` constructor on `globalThis`
- #2575 - implement DOM Event constructors and dispatch surface
- #2576 - expose WebCrypto namespace and constructors
- #2579 - expose Performance classes from `perf_hooks` / globals
- #2586 / #2601 - URL/URLSearchParams and URLPattern constructor/global identity

## Implementation boundary

- Install global function/constructor values with Node-compatible descriptors and identity, not placeholder constructors.
- Ensure `globalThis` constructors match module exports where Node does, e.g. `node:buffer`.Blob/File, `node:worker_threads` messaging constructors, `node:crypto`.webcrypto, and `node:perf_hooks` constructors.
- Complete Fetch Body methods and FormData behavior enough for multipart/form-url-encoded request and response workflows.
- Implement DOM Event/EventTarget dispatch, listener options, event subclasses, and DOMException shape used by Fetch/WebSocket/Abort APIs.
- Align WebSocket constructor/prototype/static constants and EventTarget-style instance behavior.
- Align WebCrypto and Performance constructor identity, singleton namespaces, and `instanceof` behavior.
- Keep unsupported browser-only or Bun-only globals out of scope unless Node exposes them.

## Verification

- `./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module globals`
- `./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module fetch`
- Focused supporting suites: `buffer/blob-file`, `crypto/webcrypto`, `perf_hooks`, `worker_threads`, and URL fixtures where constructor identity is touched.
- Add small probes for descriptor/identity checks such as `globalThis.Response === Response`, `require("node:buffer").File === globalThis.File`, `require("node:crypto").webcrypto === globalThis.crypto`, and `require("node:perf_hooks").PerformanceObserver === globalThis.PerformanceObserver` where Node expects identity.

## Notes

This is deliberately a Node API compatibility issue even though most names live on `globalThis`: modern Node packages feature-detect and instantiate them without importing a `node:*` module. This issue should not revive browser-only or Bun-only globals.

## Summary

Current `origin/main` has broad `node:os` manifest coverage, but it still omits the two process-priority APIs that Node exports: `os.getPriority([pid])` and `os.setPriority([pid, ]priority)`. The local node-suite already contains a focused priority fixture, so this is a concrete Node API compatibility gap rather than a Test262 item.

## Local evidence

- Baseline checked against `origin/main` because this worktree branch is behind main.
- Node v25.9.0 exports both `getPriority` and `setPriority` from `node:os`.
- `git show origin/main:crates/perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs` registers the rest of the current `os` surface, including `availableParallelism`, `endianness`, `machine`, `version`, `devNull`, and `constants`, but has no `method("os", "getPriority", ...)` or `method("os", "setPriority", ...)` rows.
- `docs/runtime-parity.md` lists both APIs under `node:os`.
- `test-parity/node-suite/os/methods/priority.ts` already probes `os.getPriority()`, bad-pid handling, and the one-argument `os.setPriority(priority)` overload.
- Existing issue search for `node:os getPriority setPriority priority` did not find an open tracker.

## Expected Node-compatible surface

- `import { getPriority, setPriority } from "node:os"` passes the manifest/import gate.
- `os.getPriority()` reads the current process priority.
- `os.getPriority(pid)` handles valid pids and returns Node-compatible errors for invalid or unavailable process ids.
- `os.setPriority(priority)` applies priority to the current process using Node overload rules.
- `os.setPriority(pid, priority)` applies priority to the selected process where the host platform allows it.
- Priority range and type validation should use Node-shaped errors, especially for values outside the supported `-20..19` range and non-number arguments.

## Suggested implementation cut

- Add manifest rows and declaration output for `os.getPriority` and `os.setPriority`.
- Add runtime/native dispatch that maps to host process-priority APIs where supported.
- On unsupported host behavior, prefer Node-compatible errors over silent no-op behavior.
- Promote or wire `test-parity/node-suite/os/methods/priority.ts` into the verification path for this issue.

## Verification

- Run the focused node-suite OS priority fixture, not Test262: `./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module os --filter priority`.
- Also run the generated API manifest/declaration drift checks if the PR changes manifest rows.

## Notes

I did not run the fixture in this checkout because the filesystem is almost full, and I intentionally avoided Test262 per the current investigation scope.

## Summary

The `node:net` port validation fix appears to have landed in `crates/perry-ext-net`, but the in-stdlib fallback path still coerces invalid ports with `as u16`. As a result, the no-auto/stdlib path still accepts invalid `net.connect` / `Socket#connect` ports that Node rejects synchronously with `RangeError [ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT]`.

This is the same API behavior tracked in the broader #2013 / closed #3639 area, but the local source now shows a split implementation: the extension backend calls the validation helper, while `crates/perry-stdlib/src/net/mod.rs` still bypasses it.

## Local evidence

Run on local `perry 0.5.1044` from commit `fdc73d06dc2015e2e295e5e2c95519c526eb7eff`:

```sh
PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1 PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1 target/release/perry test-parity/node-suite/net/validation/connect-port.ts -o /tmp/perry_net_connect_port
/tmp/perry_net_connect_port
node --experimental-strip-types test-parity/node-suite/net/validation/connect-port.ts
```

Observed diff from the net validation fixture:

```diff
-connect -1 => RangeError ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT | Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (-1).
-connect 65536 => RangeError ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT | Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (65536).
-connect 70000 => RangeError ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT | Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (70000).
-connect NaN => RangeError ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT | Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (NaN).
-connect 2.5 => RangeError ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT | Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (2.5).
-connect({port}) -1 => RangeError ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT | Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (-1).
-connect({port}) 99999 => RangeError ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT | Port should be >= 0 and < 65536. Received type number (99999).
+connect -1 => NO THROW
+connect 65536 => NO THROW
+connect 70000 => NO THROW
+connect NaN => NO THROW
+connect 2.5 => NO THROW
+connect({port}) -1 => NO THROW
+connect({port}) 99999 => NO THROW
```

The broader 8-fixture net mini-run was intentionally run with `PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1` because the workspace only had about 1.6 GiB free, so the 7 compile/link failures from that run are not being classified here. This issue is limited to the one fixture that compiled and produced a runtime output mismatch in the stdlib path.

## Source pointers

The shared validator exists in `crates/perry-runtime/src/net_validate.rs`:

- `js_net_validate_connect_port(...)` throws `ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT` for numeric ports outside `[0, 65536)`.
- `js_net_validate_listen_port(...)` covers `server.listen(...)`.

`crates/perry-ext-net/src/lib.rs` correctly calls the validator before coercing:

- options-object `net.connect({ port })`: validates before `p as u16`
- positional `net.connect(port, host)`: calls `js_net_validate_connect_port(arg1_f64)`
- `Socket#connect(port, host)`: calls `js_net_validate_connect_port(port)`

But `crates/perry-stdlib/src/net/mod.rs` still coerces directly:

- options-object `net.connect({ port })`: `Some(p) => p as u16`
- positional `net.connect(port, host)`: `let port = arg1_f64 as u16`
- `Socket#connect(port, host)`: `let port = port as u16`

## Expected behavior

The stdlib/no-auto path should use the same validation helper before truncating ports, so invalid numeric ports throw synchronously like Node and like the ext-net path intends.

## Acceptance criteria

- `PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1 ./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module net --filter validation/connect-port` passes.
- `crates/perry-stdlib/src/net/mod.rs` no longer silently truncates invalid numeric ports before `net.connect(...)` / `Socket#connect(...)` side effects.
- The behavior stays aligned with the ext-net path and #3639's intended acceptance criteria.

```text
SUMMARY total=32 pass=31 diff=1 compile_fail=0 node_fail=0 run_fail=0
DIFF tty/classes/readstream-constructor-errors
```

Diff:

```diff
-readstream: boolean function
+readstream: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED
 writestream: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED
 bad readstream: RangeError ERR_INVALID_FD
```

The fd context matters. With stdin coming from a pipe, current Node constructs the read stream:

```bash
printf 'x\n' | node --experimental-strip-types test-parity/node-suite/tty/classes/readstream-constructor-errors.ts
```

Node output:

```text
readstream: boolean function
writestream: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED
bad readstream: RangeError ERR_INVALID_FD
```

Perry output under the parity harness:

```text
readstream: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED
writestream: SystemError ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED
bad readstream: RangeError ERR_INVALID_FD
```

When stdin is `/dev/null`, Node also throws for `ReadStream(0)`, so the fixture needs the piped-stdin shape used by the suite loop. The compatibility gap is specifically the pipe-backed fd 0 case.

## Likely area

`crates/perry-runtime/src/tty.rs::js_tty_read_stream_new` calls `validate_tty_fd(fd)`, and `validate_tty_fd` throws `ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED` whenever `isatty(fd)` is false. Node's `ReadStream(0)` behavior is more permissive for a pipe-backed stdin fd than Perry's current `isatty` gate.

## Acceptance

- `test-parity/node-suite/tty/classes/readstream-constructor-errors.ts` passes under the suite harness.
- With stdin as a pipe, `new tty.ReadStream(0)` returns an object where `typeof rs.isRaw === "boolean"` and `typeof rs.setRawMode === "function"`.
- `new tty.WriteStream(1)` in the same redirected-output harness continues to throw `ERR_TTY_INIT_FAILED`, matching Node.
- Non-numeric fd validation remains intact: `new tty.ReadStream("0" as any)` throws `RangeError` with `ERR_INVALID_FD`.
payload.title: node:tty: ReadStream rejects piped stdin where Node constructs a readable TTY stream object

## Summary

`fs.unlinkSync`, callback `fs.unlink`, and `fs.promises.unlink` now correctly surface errors for directory inputs, but the error `code` is still not Node-compatible. On this macOS host, Node reports `EPERM`; Perry reports `EACCES` across all three forms.

This is the remaining narrow failure from the unlink error-propagation work. The older trackers #2736 and #3619 are closed, and there does not appear to be an open granular leaf issue for the current code mismatch.

## Local evidence

Full local `node-suite/fs` sweep on `perry 0.5.1044`:

```text
SUMMARY total=125 pass=123 diff=1 compile_fail=0 node_fail=1 run_fail=0
DIFF fs/unlink-errors
```

The `node_fail=1` is unrelated fixture drift: `fs/rmdir/recursive-options` uses `rmdir({ recursive: true })`, which current Node rejects before Perry is involved.

Focused fixture:

```bash
./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module fs --filter unlink-errors
```

or directly:

```bash
env PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1 PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1 target/release/perry test-parity/node-suite/fs/unlink-errors.ts -o /tmp/perry_fs_unlink_errors
node --experimental-strip-types test-parity/node-suite/fs/unlink-errors.ts
/tmp/perry_fs_unlink_errors
```

Relevant diff:

```diff
-sync dir code ok: true
+sync dir code ok: false
-callback dir code ok: true
+callback dir code ok: false
-promise dir code ok: true
+promise dir code ok: false
```

Minimal repro from the same host:

```ts
import * as fs from "node:fs";
import * as fsp from "node:fs/promises";

const dir = "/tmp/perry_fs_unlink_dir_code_probe";
try { fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); } catch {}
fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });

function show(label: string, err: any) {
  console.log(label, err instanceof Error, err && err.code, err && err.syscall, err && err.path === dir);
}

try { fs.unlinkSync(dir); } catch (err) { show("sync", err); }
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => fs.unlink(dir, (err) => { show("callback", err); resolve(); }));
try { await fsp.unlink(dir); } catch (err) { show("promise", err); }
```

Observed:

```text
Node:
sync true EPERM unlink true
callback true EPERM unlink true
promise true EPERM unlink true

Perry:
sync true EACCES unlink true
callback true EACCES unlink true
promise true EACCES unlink true
```

## Likely area

`crates/perry-runtime/src/fs/mod.rs::js_fs_unlink_result` routes the raw `fs::remove_file` error through `build_fs_error_value`. The syscall/path propagation is now correct, but the directory-input error code mapping differs from Node on this platform.

## Acceptance

- `test-parity/node-suite/fs/unlink-errors.ts` passes byte-identically against Node.
- Directory inputs through `fs.unlinkSync`, callback `fs.unlink`, and `fs.promises.unlink` expose a Node-compatible `code` (`EPERM` on macOS, `EISDIR` where Node reports that), while preserving `syscall === "unlink"` and the original `path`.
- Missing-path unlink errors and successful removals remain green across sync/callback/promise forms.
payload.title: node:fs: unlink directory errors report EACCES instead of Node-compatible EPERM/EISDIR

## Summary

`url.pathToFileURL()` currently resolves a relative path ending in `/` to a `file:` URL without the trailing directory slash. Node preserves that slash, so Perry serializes relative directory paths as if they were files.

This is still reproducible on local `perry 0.5.1044`; the older tracker #3624 is closed and there does not appear to be an open leaf issue for the remaining runtime mismatch.

## Repro

Existing fixture:

```bash
env PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1 PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1 target/release/perry test-parity/node-suite/url/module/path-to-file-url-relative.ts -o /tmp/perry_probe_url
node --experimental-strip-types test-parity/node-suite/url/module/path-to-file-url-relative.ts
/tmp/perry_probe_url
```

Minimal case:

```ts
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
console.log(pathToFileURL("relative/").href);
```

Observed locally:

```text
Node:  file:///Users/dutchess/Documents/PerryTS/perry/relative/
Perry: file:///Users/dutchess/Documents/PerryTS/perry/relative
```

The rest of the fixture cases matched Node in the same sweep:

```text
SUMMARY total=63 pass=62 diff=1 compile_fail=0 node_fail=0
DIFF url/module/path-to-file-url-relative
```

## Expected

`pathToFileURL("relative/").href` should preserve the trailing slash after resolving the relative directory path, matching Node.

## Likely area

`crates/perry-runtime/src/url/node_compat.rs::js_url_path_to_file_url` calls `crate::path::resolve_posix_str(&path)` before encoding. That normalization appears to strip the trailing `/`, so the later percent-encoding/URL construction cannot distinguish `relative` from `relative/`.

## Acceptance

- `test-parity/node-suite/url/module/path-to-file-url-relative.ts` passes byte-identically against Node.
- A focused regression covers at least `"relative/"`, `"relative/path"`, `"./relative/../target #?.txt"`, and `""`.
- The fix keeps existing `fileURLToPath()` / `pathToFileURL()` special-character and absolute-path behavior green.

## Summary

`process.getBuiltinModule(id)` returns placeholder native-module objects for several builtin modules instead of Node-shaped module namespaces. The returned objects only enumerate `__module__`, while Node returns the same public builtin namespace users would get through `require()`/builtin lookup.

This is related to #3668, but broader/different: #3668 covers stale `buffer` and `timers` keys on otherwise-useful returned objects. This issue covers modules where Perry currently returns only the placeholder namespace object.

Affected modules from the local probe:

- `url`
- `worker_threads`
- `stream`
- `cluster`
- `https`
- `http2`
- `child_process`

## Local evidence

Current checkout:

- `target/release/perry --version` -> `perry 0.5.1044`
- `target/release/perry --print-api-manifest=json` -> 95 modules / 2062 entries
- Node probe used Node v25.9.0

Probe:

```ts
const mods = ["url", "worker_threads", "stream", "cluster", "https", "http2", "child_process"];
for (const name of mods) {
  const mod: any = process.getBuiltinModule(name);
  const keys = mod && (typeof mod === "object" || typeof mod === "function")
    ? Object.keys(mod).sort().join(",")
    : String(mod);
  console.log(name + ":", keys);
}
```

Node v25.9.0 prints real namespace surfaces, for example:

```text
url: URL,URLPattern,URLSearchParams,Url,domainToASCII,domainToUnicode,fileURLToPath,fileURLToPathBuffer,format,parse,pathToFileURL,resolve,resolveObject,urlToHttpOptions
worker_threads: BroadcastChannel,MessageChannel,MessagePort,SHARE_ENV,Worker,getEnvironmentData,isInternalThread,isMainThread,isMarkedAsUntransferable,locks,markAsUncloneable,markAsUntransferable,moveMessagePortToContext,parentPort,postMessageToThread,receiveMessageOnPort,resourceLimits,setEnvironmentData,threadId,threadName,workerData
stream: Duplex,PassThrough,Readable,Stream,Transform,Writable,_isArrayBufferView,_isUint8Array,_uint8ArrayToBuffer,addAbortSignal,compose,destroy,duplexPair,finished,getDefaultHighWaterMark,isDestroyed,isDisturbed,isErrored,isReadable,isWritable,pipeline,promises,setDefaultHighWaterMark
cluster: SCHED_NONE,SCHED_RR,Worker,_events,_eventsCount,_maxListeners,disconnect,fork,isMaster,isPrimary,isWorker,schedulingPolicy,settings,setupMaster,setupPrimary,workers
https: Agent,Server,createServer,get,globalAgent,request
http2: Http2ServerRequest,Http2ServerResponse,connect,constants,createSecureServer,createServer,getDefaultSettings,getPackedSettings,getUnpackedSettings,performServerHandshake,sensitiveHeaders
child_process: ChildProcess,_forkChild,exec,execFile,execFileSync,execSync,fork,spawn,spawnSync
```

Perry compiles and runs the same probe with `PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1 PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1` and prints only placeholder keys:

```text
url: __module__
worker_threads: __module__
stream: __module__
cluster: __module__
https: __module__
http2: __module__
child_process: __module__
```

## Source context

`crates/perry-runtime/src/process.rs` implements `process.getBuiltinModule(id)` by normalizing the id and returning:

```rust
crate::object::js_create_native_module_namespace(module_name.as_ptr(), module_name.len())
```

`crates/perry-runtime/src/object/native_module.rs` materializes that native module namespace object with a single enumerable key:

```rust
// Create a keys array with one key: "__module__"
```

That placeholder is enough for static native-module property dispatch in some paths, but it is not a Node-compatible returned module namespace for code that inspects or dynamically reads properties from `process.getBuiltinModule()`.

The existing focused fixture `test-parity/node-suite/process/methods/get-builtin-module.ts` only checks a small subset (`fs`, `os`, `path`, `timers.setTimeout`, unknown ids, invalid ids), so it misses placeholder-only namespaces for these modules.

## Related issues

- #3668: stale `buffer`/`timers` properties on `getBuiltinModule()` return values.
- #3746: invalid named import overclaims for several transport m

## Summary

Several transport/process-adjacent Node core modules advertise names as top-level ESM exports in Perry even though Node does not expose those bindings. Some of these rows exist to support member/static dispatch or internal class filtering, but the same manifest/declaration surface currently lets invalid Node programs pass Perry's import/check layer.

This is a focused follow-up to #3709 for a concrete module cluster:

- `node:https`: `ClientRequest`, `IncomingMessage`, `ServerResponse`
- `node:http2`: `Http2SecureServer`
- `node:child_process`: `Stream`
- `node:cluster`: `on`, `addListener`, `worker`
- `node:stream`: `from`, `fromWeb`, `toWeb`, `prototype`

## Local evidence

Current checkout:

- `target/release/perry --version` -> `perry 0.5.1044`
- `target/release/perry --print-api-manifest=json` -> 95 modules / 2062 entries
- Node probe used Node v25.9.0

Probe:

```ts
import { ClientRequest, IncomingMessage, ServerResponse } from "node:https";
import { Http2SecureServer } from "node:http2";
import { Stream } from "node:child_process";
import { on, addListener, worker } from "node:cluster";
import { from, fromWeb, toWeb, prototype } from "node:stream";

console.log("https:", typeof ClientRequest, typeof IncomingMessage, typeof ServerResponse);
console.log("http2:", typeof Http2SecureServer);
console.log("child_process:", typeof Stream);
console.log("cluster:", typeof on, typeof addListener, typeof worker);
console.log("stream:", typeof from, typeof fromWeb, typeof toWeb, typeof prototype);
```

Node v25.9.0 rejects before execution:

```text
SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:https' does not provide an export named 'ClientRequest'
```

`perry check` accepts the same file with no diagnostics:

```json
{"type":"summary","success":true,"files_checked":1,"errors":0,"warnings":0,"hints":0,"deps_checked":false,"compilation_guaranteed":false,"fixable_issues":0,"fixes_applied":0,"files_modified":0}
```

Node namespace inspection confirms the names are not module exports:

```text
node:https ClientRequest false undefined
node:https IncomingMessage false undefined
node:https ServerResponse false undefined
node:http2 Http2SecureServer false undefined
node:child_process Stream false undefined
node:cluster on false undefined
node:cluster addListener false undefined
node:cluster worker false undefined
node:stream from false undefined
node:stream fromWeb false undefined
node:stream toWeb false undefined
node:stream prototype false undefined
```

## Source context

The manifest currently records these as module-level classes/properties/methods. Examples:

```rust
property("child_process", "Stream"),
class("https", "ClientRequest"),
class("https", "IncomingMessage"),
class("https", "ServerResponse"),
class("http2", "Http2SecureServer"),
property("cluster", "worker"),
property("stream", "prototype"),
method("stream", "from", false, None),
method("stream", "toWeb", false, None),
method("stream", "fromWeb", false, None),
```

The comments near the `stream.prototype` and `stream.from` rows say they are there for dispatch/gate compatibility, for example `Stream.prototype` reads and `Readable.from` routing. That is useful metadata, but it should not imply a Node-compatible top-level ESM named export.

Generated declarations currently inherit the invalid top-level shape, e.g. `docs/api/perry.d.ts` declares `child_process.Stream`, `http2.Http2SecureServer`, `https.ClientRequest`, and top-level `stream.from/fromWeb/toWeb/prototype` exports.

## Related issues

- #3709 tracks the broad export-hygiene problem for object/class members promoted to invalid named exports.
- #3695 covers `node:https` exports that Node does expose (`request`, `get`, `Agent`) but Perry resolves as `undefined`; this issue is for extra names Node does not export at all.
- #3742, #3743, and #3745 cover other concrete overclaim clusters (`tty`, `process`, and Perry-only helper exports).

## Acceptance sketch

- Perry rejects invalid named imports for this cluste

payload.body:
## Summary

Perry advertises and accepts a few helper APIs as top-level Node ESM named exports even though Node does not expose those bindings:

- `node:url`: `createObjectURL`, `revokeObjectURL`
- `node:worker_threads`: `getWorkerData`

These helpers may be useful internally or as Perry convenience shims, but in Node compatibility metadata they let Perry compile programs that Node rejects at module instantiation.

This is related to #3709's broad export-hygiene work, but it is a focused Perry-extension/alias cleanup rather than a missing implementation of the underlying capability.

## Local evidence

Current checkout:

- `target/release/perry --version` -> `perry 0.5.1044`
- `target/release/perry --print-api-manifest=json` -> 95 modules / 2062 entries
- Node probe used Node v25.9.0

### `node:url`

Probe:

```ts
import { createObjectURL, revokeObjectURL } from "node:url";
console.log("url helper types:", typeof createObjectURL, typeof revokeObjectURL);
```

Node rejects it:

```text
SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:url' does not provide an export named 'createObjectURL'
```

Perry accepts it:

```text
perry check: errors=0 warnings=0
perry compile/run: url helper types: function function
```

The Node-compatible form is the `URL` class static:

```ts
import { URL } from "node:url";
console.log(typeof URL.createObjectURL, typeof URL.revokeObjectURL); // function function
```

### `node:worker_threads`

Probe:

```ts
import { getWorkerData, workerData } from "node:worker_threads";
console.log("worker data types:", typeof getWorkerData, workerData === null || typeof workerData !== "undefined");
```

Node rejects it:

```text
SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:worker_threads' does not provide an export named 'getWorkerData'
```

Perry accepts it:

```text
perry check: errors=0 warnings=0
perry compile/run: worker data types: function false
```

Node's valid main-thread binding is the `workerData` export, which is `null` on the main thread.

## Source context

Manifest source currently registers the non-Node top-level helpers:

```rust
method("url", "createObjectURL", false, None),
method("url", "revokeObjectURL", false, None),
method("worker_threads", "getWorkerData", false, None),
```

Generated declarations expose the same invalid named-import shape:

```ts
declare module "url" {
  export function createObjectURL(...args: any[]): any;
  export function revokeObjectURL(...args: any[]): any;
}

declare module "worker_threads" {
  export const workerData: any;
  export function getWorkerData(...args: any[]): any;
}
```

Related issues:

- #3682 tracks missing `node:url` namespace tail (`URLPattern`, `Url`, `resolveObject`), but not removal/reclassification of object-URL helper overclaims.
- #3395/#3710 track real `worker_threads` state/messaging semantics, but not the non-Node `getWorkerData` named export.
- #3709 tracks the broader class/object-member-to-module-export hygiene pattern.

## Acceptance sketch

- `import { createObjectURL } from "node:url"`, `import { revokeObjectURL } from "node:url"`, and `import { getWorkerData } from "node:worker_threads"` are rejected in a Node-compatible way by check/compile/import-shape tests.
- Node-valid forms keep working:
  - `URL.createObjectURL(...)` and `URL.revokeObjectURL(...)` where object URL support exists.
  - `import { workerData } from "node:worker_threads"` and namespace/default access to `workerData` with Node-compatible values.
- If Perry wants to keep these convenience helpers, move/document them outside the Node core compatibility namespace rather than advertising them as `node:url` or `node:worker_threads` named exports.
- Generated `.d.ts`, Markdown reference, and manifest/radar checks stop treating these as Node top-level exports.
- Add small negative import-shape fixtures for `url` and `worker_threads` so the overclaims do not regress.
payload.title: node:url/node:worker_threads: Perry-only helper exports are accepted as Node named imports
