## Summary

`Proxy` `apply` and `construct` trap dispatch is broken / incomplete. **51 test262
`built-ins/Proxy` cases fail at runtime.** The existing #2768 covers
`Reflect.construct` only — Proxy's own trap behavior is untracked.

## Evidence

From a test262 parity sweep (2026-05-31), `built-ins/Proxy` runtime-fails:

- `apply/call-parameters.js` — TypeError: value is not a function
- `apply/call-result.js` — TypeError: value is not a function
- `apply/null-handler.js` — (no output / crash)
- `apply/return-abrupt.js` — TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')
- `apply/trap-is-missing-target-is-proxy.js` — value is not a function
- `apply/trap-is-not-callable.js` — Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')
- `apply/trap-is-null.js`, `apply/trap-is-undefined.js`,
  `apply/trap-is-undefined-no-property.js` — value is not a function
- `construct/call-parameters.js` — "trap context is the handler object" SameValue mismatch

## Failure modes observed

1. **Trap absent / null / undefined** → Perry throws "value is not a function"
   instead of forwarding the operation to the target (spec: a missing trap means
   the default behavior runs on the target).
2. **Trap present** → trap not invoked with the correct `this` (handler) and
   argument list; "trap context is the handler object" assertion fails.
3. **Abrupt completion / not-callable target** → "Cannot read properties of
   undefined (reading 'name')" instead of a proper TypeError.

## Repro

```js
const p = new Proxy(function () { return 42; }, {});  // no apply trap
console.log(p(1, 2, 3));   // should be 42 (forwards to target); Perry: "value is not a function"

const p2 = new Proxy(function () {}, {
  apply(target, thisArg, args) { return args.length; }
});
console.log(p2(1, 2, 3));  // should be 3
```

## Suggested scope

Implement Proxy `apply`/`construct` exotic behavior: when the trap is
missing/undefined, fall through to the target's `[[Call]]`/`[[Construct]]`; when
present, invoke with `(target, thisArg, argArray)` and the handler as `this`.
Likely lives alongside the existing Proxy get/set/has trap handling in the runtime.

---
*Filed from the parity-gap radar (`scripts/parity_gap_report.py`). Cluster: 51
`built-ins/Proxy` runtime failures. Related: #2768 (Reflect.construct).*
payload.title: runtime: implement Proxy apply/construct trap dispatch

## Summary

Built-in functions and constructors are still missing own `name` / `length` data
properties across a wide swath of the standard library. Test262 `verifyProperty`
checks fail with **"name should be an own property"** / **"length should be an own
property"** on ~131 cases spanning ~25 categories.

This is a **follow-on to the now-closed #3143** ("Built-in property descriptors &
.name/.length conformance"). That issue landed partial coverage, but a full
parity sweep shows the conformance is far from complete — many builtins still
lack the own `name`/`length` properties (with the spec-required
`{writable:false, enumerable:false, configurable:true}` descriptor shape).

## Evidence

From a test262 + node-core parity sweep (2026-05-31): **131 failures** with this
exact signature. Affected categories (top): Function (9), RegExp (6), Math (6),
Reflect (6), TypedArrayConstructors (6), NativeErrors (5), Date (5), Object (5),
plus single/double-digit hits across ArrayBuffer, AsyncFunction, BigInt,
DataView, Array, Map, Set, WeakMap, WeakSet, Promise, and more.

Representative cases:
- `built-ins/Array/from/Array.from-name.js` — "name should be an own property"
- `built-ins/Array/from/Array.from_arity.js` — "length should be an own property"
- `built-ins/ArrayBuffer/isView/{name,length}.js`
- `built-ins/AsyncFunction/{instance-has-name,instance-length}.js`
- `built-ins/BigInt/asIntN/{name,length}.js`, `asUintN/{name,length}.js`
- `built-ins/Reflect/apply/{name,length}.js`, `defineProperty/{name,length}.js`
- `built-ins/DataView/{name,length}.js`

## Repro

```js
// All of these should print the spec values; today the own-property lookup fails.
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Array.from, 'name'));   // {value:'from', writable:false, enumerable:false, configurable:true}
console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(BigInt.asIntN, 'length')); // length 2
console.log(Reflect.apply.name, Reflect.apply.length);
```

## Why it's high-leverage

This is a single semantic (own `name`/`length` descriptors on builtins) that, once
generalized, clears ~131 failures at once. It also unblocks `verifyProperty`-based
assertions in many other categories that currently abort early on this check.

## Suggested scope

Audit how `.name`/`.length` are installed on builtin function/constructor objects
(the mechanism #3143 introduced) and extend it to cover every builtin
function/constructor uniformly, with the correct descriptor attributes.

---
*Filed from the parity-gap radar (`scripts/parity_gap_report.py`). Cluster: 131
failures, "name/length should be an own property".*
payload.title: runtime: complete own name/length descriptors on builtins (follow-on to closed #3143)

## Summary

Current local `node-suite/test` parity shows `node:test` still diverges in three user-visible areas that are easy for packages and smoke tests to hit:

- default/named `test` export identity and callable shape
- `mock.timers` state, fake-clock behavior, and validation errors
- snapshot helper validation and executable snapshot assertions

This is a focused follow-up under the broader `node:test` epic #3602. It is also important because prior granular issues #3153 and #3154 are closed with a verification note saying `node-suite/test` passed, but the current worktree reproduces failures for mock timers and snapshots.

## Current local evidence

Run on 2026-05-31:

```sh
PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1 ./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module test
```

Result: 1 pass, 3 parity fail, 0 compile fail (`test-parity/reports/parity_report_20260531_025909.json`).

Failing fixtures:

- `node-suite/test/imports/module-shape`
- `node-suite/test/mock-timers/basic`
- `node-suite/test/snapshots/snapshot`

## Observed diffs

### Module default export shape

Node treats the default export as the callable `test` function and keeps it identical to the named `test` export. Perry currently exposes an object as default and the identity differs:

```diff
-test default: function
-test identity: same
+test default: object
+test identity: different
```

### Mock timers behavior and validation

Node rejects `mock.timers.tick()` before `enable()`, freezes/advances `Date`, drains scheduled timers with `tick()` and `runAll()`, validates bad APIs and bad `setTime()` input. Perry currently accepts invalid calls but does not actually fake time or fire the scheduled callbacks:

```diff
-pre tick: ERR_INVALID_STATE
-start: 1000 1970-01-01T00:00:01.000Z
-after5: ["interval:1005"]
-after10: ["interval:1005","timeout:1010","interval:1010"]
-afterRunAll: ["interval:1005","timeout:1010","interval:1010","runAll:1035"]
-afterSetTime: 2000
-bad api: ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE
-bad setTime: ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
+pre tick: NO_THROW
+start: <real current time>
+after5: []
+after10: []
+afterRunAll: []
+afterSetTime: <real current time>
+bad api: NO_THROW
+bad setTime: NO_THROW
```

### Snapshot helper validation and execution

Node validates `snapshot.setDefaultSnapshotSerializers()` and `snapshot.setResolveSnapshotPath()` argument types and then runs a snapshot test to completion. Perry currently accepts invalid configuration and exits before the fixture reaches the test assertion output:

```diff
-serializers invalid: ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
-resolver invalid: ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
-snapshot assertions: ok
+serializers invalid: NO_THROW
+resolver invalid: NO_THROW
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `import test, { test as namedTest } from "node:test"` exposes a function-valued default export identical to the named test export.
- `mock.timers` matches Node for disabled-state errors, `enable({ apis, now })`, `tick`, `runAll`, `setTime`, `reset`, and validation error codes covered by `node-suite/test/mock-timers/basic`.
- Snapshot configuration helpers validate argument types like Node and snapshot/fileSnapshot assertions run to deterministic completion for `node-suite/test/snapshots/snapshot`.
- `./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module test` reaches 4/4 parity pass without removing the fixtures.

## Related issues

- Broad epic: #3602
- Prior mock timers issue, currently closed: #3153
- Prior snapshot issue, currently closed: #3154

## Summary

Perry's `Text` widget currently has no way to set horizontal text alignment (equivalent to CSS `text-align`). The underlying platform APIs all support this, but Perry doesn't expose it.

## Evidence

All three platforms have the capability but none is wired to a user-callable FFI function:

| Platform | Underlying API | Used internally? | Exposed to user? |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| macOS | `NSTextField.setAlignment:` | ✅ toast.rs, chart.rs, bottom_nav.rs | ❌ |
| iOS | `UILabel.setTextAlignment:` | ✅ toast.rs | ❌ |
| Android | `TextView.setGravity(Gravity.CENTER_HORIZONTAL)` | ✅ image.rs, qrcode.rs | ❌ |

Verified by inspecting:
- `crates/perry-ui-macos/src/lib_ffi/core_widgets.rs` — all `perry_ui_text_set_*` functions listed, no alignment
- `crates/perry-ui-ios/src/ffi/widgets_basic.rs` — same
- `crates/perry-ui-android/src/` — same

## Proposed API

```typescript
// perry/ui type declaration
export function textSetTextAlignment(widget: Widget, alignment: number): void;
```

Alignment values (follow NSTextAlignment / UITextAlignment conventions):
- `0` = left
- `1` = right  
- `2` = center
- `4` = natural (follows locale direction)

## Current Workaround

Without this API, centering text requires wrapping in an extra container:

```typescript
// Workaround: wrap Text in a VStack with CenterX alignment
function centeredText(content: string, parentWidth: number): Widget {
    const t = Text(content);
    const col = VStack(0, [t]);
    stackSetAlignment(col, 9);        // NSLayoutAttribute.centerX
    widgetSetWidth(col, parentWidth); // required reference width
    return col;
}
```

This adds an extra layout layer for what should be a single property.

## Implementation Notes

The pattern already exists in the codebase — Perry uses `setTextAlignment` internally. Adding the public binding would follow the same 3-step pattern as other text setters:

1. **Rust impl** (`crates/perry-ui-macos/src/lib_ffi/core_widgets.rs`):
```rust
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn perry_ui_text_set_text_alignment(handle: i64, alignment: i64) {
    if let Some(view) = get_widget(handle) {
        unsafe { let _: () = msg_send![&*view, setAlignment: alignment]; }
    }
}
```

2. **Dispatch table** (`crates/perry-dispatch/src/ui_table.rs`): add a `MethodRow` entry

3. **JS codegen** (`crates/perry-codegen-js/src/emit/calls.rs`): add the method name → runtime symbol mapping

Android would use `setGravity` with the appropriate gravity flags for horizontal alignment.
payload.title: feat(ui): expose textSetTextAlignment API for Text widget

```bash
./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module fs --filter unlink-errors
```

- 0 pass, 1 parity fail
- report: `test-parity/reports/parity_report_20260531_021540.json`
- fixture: `test-parity/node-suite/fs/unlink-errors.ts`

Diff from the saved runner outputs:

```diff
 sync dir is Error: true
-sync dir code ok: true
+sync dir code ok: false

-callback dir code ok: true
+callback dir code ok: false

+promise dir code ok: false

```

The missing-path cases now match Node (`ENOENT`), and successful sync/callback/promise removals still work. The remaining gap is directory unlink error-code parity.

## Dedupe / relation to existing work

- #3590 is the broad fs/fs-promises compatibility umbrella.
- #2736 tracked the original `fs.unlink` error-propagation gap and was closed by #2759.
- This issue is narrower: after #2759, Perry still reports a non-Node-compatible directory error `code` for `unlink` even though `syscall` and `path` are present.
- Nearby closed removal trackers such as #2747 should be audited only if they share the same error-code mapping path.

## Acceptance criteria

- `fs.unlinkSync(directory)` throws a Node-shaped error with `code` equal to `EISDIR` or `EPERM`, `syscall === "unlink"`, and matching `path`.
- `fs.unlink(directory, cb)` passes that same error shape to the callback.
- `fs.promises.unlink(directory)` rejects with that same error shape.
- Missing-path and successful unlink behavior remain green.
- `test-parity/node-suite/fs/unlink-errors.ts` passes.


## Summary

Track operator/runtime failures in ToPrimitive, boxed primitive addition, Symbol/BigInt coercion errors, and array spread abrupt-completion propagation. These gaps affect ordinary Node.js package code that depends on JavaScript coercion and iterator error semantics.

## Evidence

Source of truth: local Test262 parity triage generated from `/Users/dutchess/Downloads/parity_gaps_report.partial.jsonl` against pinned Test262 `4249661388e5d3f92a85186213da140a6481490f`.

Cluster size: 32 rows.

Representative failures:

- `language/expressions/addition/S11.6.1_A1.js`: `TypeError: value is not a function` during addition coercion.
- boxed primitive addition cases: `new Boolean(true) + true` produces `NaN` instead of Node/Test262 result.
- unresolvable reference / Symbol / BigInt addition cases do not propagate the expected error.
- `language/expressions/array/spread-err-*.js`: spread expression/iterator errors are silently missed.

## Implementation checklist

- [ ] Apply GetValue and ToPrimitive in ECMAScript order for `+` operands.
- [ ] Support OrdinaryToPrimitive for boxed Boolean, Number, String, Date, and Function values.
- [ ] Propagate ReferenceError, TypeError, Symbol, BigInt, and user ToPrimitive errors through addition.
- [ ] Propagate abrupt completions through array spread expression evaluation, iterator acquisition, `next`, and `value` reads.
- [ ] Add focused regression fixtures for object addition and spread error paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- `+` uses `valueOf`/`toString` ordering compatible with Node for ordinary objects, Dates, functions, and boxed primitives.
- Mixed Symbol/BigInt/Number and unresolvable-reference cases throw the same class of error as Node/Test262.
- Array spread no longer swallows errors from iterator evaluation or value extraction.
- The affected Test262 rows move to pass.

## Verification


## Summary

Track Test262 failures where Perry does not materialize, describe, alias, or propagate `arguments` objects the way ECMAScript requires. This affects Node.js compatibility because Node executes these same JavaScript semantics before any `node:*` API is involved.

## Evidence

Source of truth: local Test262 parity triage generated from `/Users/dutchess/Downloads/parity_gaps_report.partial.jsonl` against pinned Test262 `4249661388e5d3f92a85186213da140a6481490f`.

Cluster size: 43 rows.

Representative failures:

- `language/arguments-object/10.6-11-b-1.js`: `0 should be an own property`
- `language/arguments-object/10.6-6-2.js`: `length should be an own property`
- `language/arguments-object/S10.6_A2.js`: `arguments doesn't exists`
- async-generator trailing-comma `arguments` cases: Perry produces no output where Node/Test262 completes

Related existing coverage to avoid duplicating:

- `#3146` covers broad spec-mandated missing throws, but does not cover arguments object materialization/aliasing as an end-to-end feature.
- Eval/dynamic-code rows are excluded under Perry's AOT policy (`#1677`, `#1678`, `#1679`).

## Implementation checklist

- [ ] Materialize ordinary non-arrow function `arguments` objects.
- [ ] Expose indexed own properties, `length`, and strict/sloppy `callee` descriptors.
- [ ] Implement mapped vs unmapped arguments aliasing for simple vs non-simple/strict parameter lists.
- [ ] Preserve `arguments` semantics in async-generator, rest-parameter, and `new.target` forms.
- [ ] Add focused regression fixtures for ordinary, strict, and async/generator forms.

## Acceptance criteria

- Functions that return or inspect `arguments` see a real object instead of an absent binding.
- `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(arguments, "length")`, indexed entries, and `callee` match Node for strict/sloppy cases.
- Parameter writes and `arguments[i]` writes alias exactly in mapped cases and remain independent in unmapped cases.
- The affected Test262 rows move from runtime-fail/diff to pass.

## Verification

```bash
cargo build --release -p perry -p perry-runtime -p perry-stdlib
```

payload.author: proggeramlug
payload.body:
Split out of #3149 (Bug 2). Bug 1 (`Object(null)` → `{}` plain-call coercion) landed in #3530; this is the remaining, riskier half.

## Bug — reassigning a function-declaration binding is ignored

```js
function G(m){ this.v = "OLD"; }
G = function(m){ this.v = "NEW"; };
new G(1).v;   // Perry "OLD"   Node "NEW"

function H(){ return "h-old"; }
H = function(){ return "h-new"; };
H();          // Perry "h-old"  Node "h-new"
```

A top-level `function` declaration's binding is treated as an immutable `FuncRef` at use sites, so a later `G = ...` reassignment doesn't take effect — `new G()` / `G()` still call the original.

## Root cause

`crates/perry-hir/src/lower/lower_expr.rs::lower_expr_assignment` (the `ast::Expr::Ident` arm) currently **discards** the RHS when the target names a function or class binding:

```rust
} else if ctx.lookup_class(&name).is_some() || ctx.lookup_func(&name).is_some() {
    // ...evaluate RHS for side effects only...
    Ok(*value)
}
```

And bare-identifier reads resolve a function name straight to `Expr::FuncRef(id)` (`lower_expr.rs:136-137`), never consulting a mutable slot.

## Sketch of a fix

Function-declaration bindings are mutable `var`-like bindings in JS. Likely shape:

1. Pre-scan the module for top-level function names that appear as an assignment target; only those need the mutable treatment (no perf/behavior change for the common, never-reassigned case).
2. For a reassigned name, give it a mutable global/local slot initialized (at hoist time) to the function as a closure value.
3. Route reads → slot load, `G = ...` → slot store, and `G()` / `new G()` → dynamic call / `NewDynamic` of the slot value.

This touches the `FuncRef` read path, call lowering, and `new` lowering — several sites with real regression surface, so it wants human review / pairing before landing on protected `main`.

## Acceptance criteria

- After `G = fn2`, both `new G()` and `G()` invoke `fn2`.
- `var f = G; G = otherFn;` — `f` keeps the old binding, `G` reflects the reassignment.
- Un-reassigned function declarations keep working with no perf/behavior regression.
- Gap test, differential vs `node --experimental-strip-types`.

Refs: #3149, #3530, Test262 radar #799, Node+TS roadmap #793.

payload.author: proggeramlug
payload.body:
## Summary

Tracking issue: **what it takes to compile a standard Express app with Perry.**

I took a textbook Express 5 app, installed real Express (`express@5.2.1`, 65 packages in the tree, all plain CommonJS/JS), and drove it through `perry compile`, removing one blocker at a time to surface the *entire* chain rather than stopping at the first error.

**Headline finding (the good news):** Express's whole dependency tree is essentially TypeScript-subset-compatible — **all 65 packages route to native compilation; none require the (removed) V8 runtime.** Modern JS like Express really does compile the same as TS here. With a handful of escape hatches + two tiny dependency shims, Perry emits an 11.6 MB native binary (`COMPILE_EXIT=0`).

**The catch:** that binary is a false positive. The compiler **tolerates 49 per-module codegen failures and links the broken objects in anyway**, so the binary **`Bus error: 10` on launch with zero output**. The real central blocker is a **codegen bug**, not the JS/TS divide.

## Repro

```ts
// app.ts
import express from 'express';
const app = express();
app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('Hello World!'));
app.get('/json', (req, res) => res.json({ message: 'hello', value: 42 }));
app.listen(3000, () => console.log('listening on port 3000'));
```

```bash
npm install express          # express@5.2.1, 65 packages
perry compile app.ts -o app_bin
```

Tested on `main` @ `bef6c3530`, macOS arm64, Apple clang 21.0.0.

## The blocker chain (in the order you hit them)

### 1. Bare `import` of a JS package → V8-removed gate
With no config, `express/index.js` (CJS) routes to the removed JS runtime:
> `Error: JavaScript runtime (V8) support has been removed... pulled in a JS runtime via: express/index.js [express]`

### 2. `#497` trust gate
Adding `perry.compilePackages: ["express"]` then trips:
> `package 'express' is in compilePackages but not in perry.allow.compilePackages`

Fix: also set `perry.allow.compilePackages`, or `PERRY_ALLOW_PERRY_FEATURES=1`.

### 3. Opt-in is **not transitive** — must enumerate all 65 packages
Even with both flags set for `express`, all 28+ transitive deps individually route to V8:
> `still routed to runtime JavaScript because they are not in perry.compilePackages: accepts, body-parser, content-disposition, ... vary`

You must list **every** package in the tree (direct + transitive) in *both* `compilePackages` and `allow.compilePackages`.

### 4. 🐛 The `"*"` wildcard is broken for compile-routing
`compilePackages: ["*"]` + `allow.compilePackages: ["*"]` passes the **trust** gate (no #497 error) but the wildcard is **not honored by native-compile routing** — `express` is treated as un-opted-in and immediately routes to V8:
```
Compile package: *
JS module: express -> .../express/index.js
Error: JavaScript runtime (V8) support has been removed... express/index.js [express]
```
So `"*"` is strictly worse than naming `"express"`. **This is a standalone bug worth fixing first** — it's the natural "compile everything" ergonomic and it silently does nothing for routing.

### 5. `new Function(...)` / `Function(...)` refused (#1677) — eval-family
With the full tree enumerated, the first *hard language* error:
- **`depd`** `index.js:436` — `new Function(...)` (builds deprecation wrappers from a code string to preserve arity).
- **`function-bind`** `implementation.js:85` — `Function(...)`. This one is **deep and ubiquitous** (pulled in by `get-intrinsic`, which nearly everything depends on).

Both are trivially replaceable with ordinary closures. `PERRY_ALLOW_EVAL=1` bypasses but yields non-functional behavior.

### 6. Unimplemented stdlib surface (#463)
After shimming depd: `buffer.hasOwnProperty is not implemented` (and likely more behind it). `PERRY_ALLOW_UNIMPLEMENTED=1` skips the whole category to surface deeper errors.

### 7. 🐛 **CENTRAL BLOCKER — codegen emits references to undefined `@perry_closure_*` globals**
With eval + unimplemented + features all bypassed and depd/functi

## Summary
`performance.markResourceTiming(...)` is callable in Perry, but it is still implemented as a no-op. Node returns a `PerformanceResourceTiming` object and appends a `resource` entry visible through `performance.getEntriesByType("resource")`; Perry returns `undefined` and records nothing.

## Node Behavior
Focused repro:

```ts
import { performance } from "node:perf_hooks";

const before = performance.getEntriesByType("resource").length;
const timingInfo: any = {
  startTime: 10,
  redirectStart: 0,
  redirectEnd: 0,
  fetchStart: 10,
  domainLookupStart: 11,
  domainLookupEnd: 12,
  connectStart: 13,
  connectEnd: 14,
  requestStart: 15,
  responseStart: 16,
  responseEnd: 20,
};

const returned: any = (performance as any).markResourceTiming(
  timingInfo,
  "https://example.test/a",
  "fetch",
  globalThis,
  "",
);
const entries: any[] = performance.getEntriesByType("resource") as any[];
const last: any = entries[entries.length - 1];

console.log("return ctor:", returned?.constructor?.name || String(returned));
console.log("count delta:", entries.length - before);
console.log("last name:", last?.name || "none");
console.log("last type:", last?.entryType || "none");
console.log("last initiator:", last?.initiatorType || "none");
console.log("last start:", last?.startTime);
```

Local Node output on 2026-05-30:

```console
return ctor: PerformanceResourceTiming
count delta: 1
last name: https://example.test/a
last type: resource
last initiator: fetch
last start: 10
```

## Summary

Node's Fetch `Headers` object is directly iterable: `headers[Symbol.iterator]` is a function, it is the same function as `headers.entries`, and `for...of` / spread over `headers` yields sorted `[name, value]` pairs. Perry currently segfaults when a focused probe tries to iterate a `Headers` instance directly.

## Node Behavior

Minimal repro:

```ts
const h = new Headers();
h.append("b", "2");
h.append("a", "1");

console.log("iterator typeof:", typeof (h as any)[Symbol.iterator]);
console.log("entries typeof:", typeof h.entries);

const viaForOf: string[] = [];
for (const [key, value] of h as any) {
  viaForOf.push(`${key}=${value}`);
}
console.log("for-of:", viaForOf.join(","));

console.log("spread:", JSON.stringify([...(h as any)]));
console.log("iterator equals entries:", (h as any)[Symbol.iterator] === h.entries);
```

Node output from `test-files/tmp_headers_iterator.ts`:

```text
iterator typeof: function
entries typeof: function
for-of: a=1,b=2
spread: [["a","1"],["b","2"]]
iterator equals entries: true
```

## Perry Behavior

Focused parity run:

- report: `test-parity/reports/parity_report_20260530_112104.json`
- fixture: `test-files/tmp_headers_iterator.ts`
- result: `parity_fail: ["tmp_headers_iterator"]`

Perry output:

```text
./run_parity_tests.sh: line 67: 82401 Segmentation fault: 11  "$@"
```

Related local evidence:

- `docs/runtime-parity-gaps.md` still lists `headers[Symbol.iterator]()` as a Web/global gap.
- `crates/perry-stdlib/src/fetch/headers.rs` comments say `for (const [k, v] of h)` should route through the `Symbol.iterator` alias to `headers.entries()`.
- `crates/perry-stdlib/src/fetch/dispatch.rs` exposes bound string-named methods such as `entries`, `keys`, and `values`, but the focused direct-iterator probe still crashes.

Duplicate searches before filing:

- `Headers Symbol.iterator segfault`
- `Headers iterator for-of spread`
- `headers[Symbol.iterator]`

Those found closed #576 for `headers.keys()` iteration, merged PR #1996 for generic untyped receiver iteration, and open #2645 for constructor init. I did not find an open issue for direct `Headers` iteration crashing.

## Summary
`timersPromises.scheduler.yield()` should yield to a later turn so already-queued promise microtasks run before the yield promise settles. Perry currently returns an already-resolved promise, so `.then()` handlers attached to `scheduler.yield()` run before later queued microtasks.

## Node Behavior
Minimal repro:

```ts
import { scheduler } from "node:timers/promises";

const events: string[] = [];
const yielded = scheduler.yield().then(() => events.push("yield"));
Promise.resolve().then(() => events.push("micro"));
events.push("sync");
await yielded;
console.log(events.join(","));
```

Node v25.9.0 output:

```text
sync,micro,yield
```

## Perry Behavior
A focused local parity probe on 2026-05-30 showed Perry resolves the yield promise too early:

```text
./run_parity_tests.sh --filter tmp_timers_promises_scheduler_yield_order
Node.js: sync,micro,yield
Perry:   sync,yield,micro
```

Report: `test-parity/reports/parity_report_20260530_101716.json`

`origin/main` source evidence points at the same behavior: `crates/perry-runtime/src/node_submodules/timers.rs::timers_promises_scheduler_yield()` constructs `js_promise_resolved(undefined)` directly instead of scheduling settlement onto a later timer/immediate turn.

## Summary

`node:http2.createSecureServer({ key, cert }, handler)` should be able to start a secure HTTP/2 server, invoke the listen callback, close cleanly, and let the process exit. Perry currently gets stuck on the node-suite secure-server fixture before any fixture output is produced.

## Node Behavior

The focused fixture is `test-parity/node-suite/http2/server/node-prefix.ts`. It writes a PEM key/cert pair to `/tmp`, imports `createSecureServer` from `node:http2`, starts a server on `127.0.0.1:19023`, then closes it from the listen callback:

```ts
const server = createSecureServer(
  { key: readFileSync(keyPath, "utf8"), cert: readFileSync(certPath, "utf8") },
  (_req: any, res: any) => {
    res.statusCode = 200;
    res.end("ok");
  },
);

server.listen({ port: 19023, host: "127.0.0.1" }, () => {
  console.log("http2 secure listening");
  server.close(() => console.log("http2 secure closed"));
});
```

Running the fixture directly with Node completes:

```console
$ node --experimental-strip-types test-parity/node-suite/http2/server/node-prefix.ts
http2 secure listening
http2 secure closed
```

## Perry Behavior

```console
$ ./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module http2
Running parity tests (backend: LLVM, suite: node-suite, module: http2)...
```

## Summary

`node:zlib` sync codecs accept JavaScript strings as data inputs in Node, encoding them as UTF-8 before compression. Perry currently accepts the call but corrupts the input/output path, so `gzipSync("hello world")` no longer round-trips through `gunzipSync()`.

## Node Behavior

Minimal repro from `test-parity/node-suite/zlib/inputs/string-direct.ts`:

```ts
import { gzipSync, gunzipSync } from "node:zlib";

const out = gunzipSync(gzipSync("hello world")).toString();
console.log("string roundtrip equal:", out === "hello world");
console.log("string roundtrip out:", out);
```

Node output:

```text
string roundtrip equal: true
string roundtrip out: hello world
```

## Perry Behavior

Current targeted parity run:

```console
$ ./run_parity_tests.sh --suite node-suite --module zlib --filter string-direct
FAIL  node-suite/zlib/inputs/string-direct (output mismatch)
       Node.js:    string roundtrip equal: true
       Perry:  string roundtrip equal: false
```

The saved Perry output shows the decompressed value is not the original string:

```text
string roundtrip equal: false
string roundtrip out: Wed Dec 31 1969 16:00:00 GMT-0800 (local)
```

The full granular zlib suite is otherwise close enough to isolate this gap:

```text
Parity Pass:   48
Parity Fail:   1
Output Mismatches:
  - node-suite/zlib/inputs/string-direct
```

Relevant implementation evidence: `crates/perry-stdlib/src/zlib.rs` sync helpers take `*const StringHeader` and route through `bytes_from_header()`, while indirect native dispatch passes `as_str_ptr(arg(0))` for `gzipSync`, `gunzipSync`, `deflateSync`, `inflateSync`, raw codecs, unzip, Brotli, and `crc32`.

## Gap

`import * as module from "node:module"` does not compile in Perry parity tests, so the Node `node:module` namespace object is unavailable before any individual API behavior can be checked.

Node exposes a namespace object for `node:module` containing static helpers/properties such as `builtinModules`, `createRequire`, `isBuiltin`, `register`, `registerHooks`, compile-cache helpers, source-map helpers, `stripTypeScriptTypes`, `syncBuiltinESMExports`, `wrap`, `wrapper`, `constants`, and `SourceMap`.

## Current Perry behavior

Running the generated parity fixture fails at compile time:

```console
$ ./run_parity_tests.sh --filter test_parity_module
FAIL  test_parity_module (compile error)

Compile Failures:
  - test_parity_module
```

The compiler rejection is the namespace-import path in `collect_modules.rs`:

```text
Could not resolve namespace import `import * as ... from "module"` in test_parity_module.ts.
Perry has no stdlib bindings for this module path, so the namespace would compile to an empty object...
```

Fixture source: `test-files/test_parity_module.ts` begins with:

```ts
import * as module from "node:module";
```

and then probes the namespace shape for the APIs above.

## Expected behavior

The namespace import should compile and produce a `module` namespace object with Node-compatible static properties and helper functions. Individual method semantics can continue to be covered by the existing granular issues, but the namespace binding itself should not block runtime parity checks.

## Related open leaves

Existing open `node:module` leaves cover individual APIs:

- #3118 builtin module metadata
- #3119 `createRequire`

- #3121 compile-cache controls

## Summary
Node accepts AES-GCM IV lengths beyond the usual 12-byte nonce by deriving the GCM initial counter block from the IV. Perry's AES-GCM encrypt path assumes a 12-byte nonce and aborts when the IV is 16 bytes.

## Node Behavior
`./run_parity_tests.sh --filter test_parity_crypto` exercises AES-256-GCM with a 16-byte IV:

```ts
const keyGcm = Buffer.from("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef", "hex");
const ivGcm = Buffer.from("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef", "hex");
const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", keyGcm, ivGcm);
cipher.setAAD(Buffer.from("aad"));
let enc = cipher.update("hello", "utf8", "hex");
enc += cipher.final("hex");
const tag = cipher.getAuthTag().toString("hex");
console.log("aes-256-gcm enc:", enc);
console.log("aes-256-gcm tag:", tag);
```

Node output:

```text
aes-256-gcm enc: 82e97b8e96
aes-256-gcm tag: c58935f5665deb54f75ee7dc0b34d61c
aes-256-gcm dec: hello
```

## Perry Behavior
The same targeted parity run currently aborts after the AES-CBC section when it reaches the 16-byte-IV GCM path:

```text
thread '<unnamed>' (...) panicked at .../generic-array-0.14.7/src/lib.rs:572:9:
assertion `left == right` failed

 right: 12
Abort trap: 6
```

payload.author: proggeramlug
payload.body:
## Summary

`String.prototype.length` undercounts by 1 for **every 3-byte-UTF-8 BMP code point that appears inside a multi-character string** (e.g. `€` U+20AC, `—` U+2014, CJK). The character is stored correctly (`charCodeAt` and `String.fromCharCode(c).length` are both right) — only the aggregate `.length` of a containing string is wrong.

JS `.length` counts UTF-16 code units; a BMP char is always exactly 1 unit regardless of its UTF-8 byte width, so Perry should match Node here.

## Repro (escape-only, no raw multibyte — safe to copy)

```ts
console.log("lit_euro=" + "a€b".length);              // Node 3, Perry 2
const mid = String.fromCharCode(0x20ac);
console.log("concat_euro=" + ("a" + mid + "b").length);   // Node 3, Perry 2  (defeats constant folding)
console.log("fromCharCode_len=" + mid.length);            // Node 1, Perry 1   (correct in isolation)
console.log("lit_eacute=" + "café".length);               // Node 4, Perry 4   (2-byte é counts correctly)
console.log("cc=" + "a€b".charCodeAt(1));            // Node 8364, Perry 8364 (char stored correctly)
```

Perry output:
```
lit_euro=2
concat_euro=2
fromCharCode_len=1
lit_eacute=4
cc=8364
```

Node (`node --experimental-strip-types`) output:
```
lit_euro=3
concat_euro=3
fromCharCode_len=1
lit_eacute=4
cc=8364
```

## Observations

- The undercount appears for both **string literals** and **runtime-concatenated** strings (`"a"+mid+"b"`), so it is the stored-string length computation, not just a constant-fold path.
- `String.fromCharCode(0x20ac).length === 1` is **correct** in isolation — the regression is specific to a 3-byte char *combined with other characters* in one string.
- 2-byte-UTF-8 chars (`é` U+00E9, → `"café".length === 4`) are correct; 1-byte ASCII is correct. So the byte-walk that derives length appears to mis-handle the 3-byte (0xE0–0xEF lead-byte) case, contributing 0 instead of 1.
- `charCodeAt` returns the right code unit, confirming the bytes are stored intact — only the length accounting is wrong.

## Impact

Affects extremely common characters: the Euro sign, em/en dashes, smart quotes, and the entire CJK/Hangul/Hiragana BMP range. Any code that slices, pads, or validates lengths of strings containing these characters will diverge from Node.

This is distinct from the documented WTF-8 lone-surrogate gap — these are well-formed BMP scalar values.

## Discovery context

Surfaced while implementing `util.toUSVString` (#2514): `toUSVString("a\uD800b")` correctly yields `"a�b"` (content byte-identical to Node), but `.length` reports 2 instead of 3 because U+FFFD is itself a 3-byte char hitting this bug. The toUSVString fix asserts on content rather than `.length` to avoid it.

## Verification note

Reproduced on a locally-built `perry` from current `main` (7f6865ca5). Repro uses `\u`/`fromCharCode` escapes only (no raw multibyte source bytes), so it is robust to editor/transport encoding.

- #3360 - `Readable.from(generator)` drops yielded chunks.


Source evidence:

## Summary

`Readable.prototype.wrap(oldStream)` should bridge a Node 0.10-style stream or EventEmitter that emits `data` and `end` into a modern Readable. # test-parity/node-suite/stream/readable/wrap-pipe-chain.ts
```text
piped: x
```

```ts
}
```

## Summary

Node's `util.inspect` export is both callable and a property-bearing function. It exposes `inspect.custom`, `inspect.defaultOptions`, `inspect.styles`, and `inspect.colors` for feature detection, custom-inspect symbols, default rendering options, and style/color tables.

Perry already has internal support for the custom inspect symbol in lowered code and formatter lookup, but the runtime `util.inspect` function itself does not expose Node's static property surface. That leaves dynamic/captured access such as `const { inspect } = require("node:util"); inspect.custom` and `inspect.defaultOptions.depth = 0` incompatible.

## Node behavior

Checked with Node v25.9.0:

```js
const { inspect } = require("node:util");

console.log(inspect.custom === Symbol.for("nodejs.util.inspect.custom"));
console.log(typeof inspect.defaultOptions, inspect.defaultOptions.depth, inspect.defaultOptions.customInspect);
console.log(typeof inspect.styles, inspect.styles.number);
console.log(Array.isArray(inspect.colors.yellow), inspect.colors.yellow.join(","));

const originalDepth = inspect.defaultOptions.depth;
inspect.defaultOptions.depth = 0;
console.log(inspect({ a: { b: 1 } }));
inspect.defaultOptions.depth = originalDepth;
```

Observed output includes:

```text
true
object 2 true
object yellow
true 33,39
{ a: [Object] }
```

## Perry evidence

- `docs/runtime-parity-gaps.md` lists `util.inspect.custom`, `util.inspect.defaultOptions`, `util.inspect.styles`, and `util.inspect.colors` as missing.
- `crates/perry-runtime/src/object/native_module.rs` synthesizes `node:util` callables including `inspect` (`("util", "inspect")`), so namespace reads produce a function value.
- `create_native_callable_export()` currently attaches a dynamic `custom` property only for `module_name == "util" && property_name == "promisify"`; there is no analogous branch for `util.inspect`.
- `get_native_module_constant()` handles `util.default`, `util.types`, `util.TextEncoder`, and `util.TextDecoder`, but not `inspect` static-property objects.
- `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_member.rs` lowers some static source patterns for `util.inspect.custom` / `inspect.custom` to `Symbol.for("nodejs.util.inspect.custom")`, which does not cover runtime property access on the actual exported function.

## Suggested PR cut

Batch this with #3281 (`node:util: callable helper and diagnostics semantics parity cut`). This is not an inspect rendering rewrite; it is callable export/static-property surface parity for `node:util`.

## Duplicate search

Checked open/closed issues and PRs for:

- `node:util inspect custom defaultOptions styles colors static properties`
- `util.inspect.defaultOptions util.inspect.colors util.inspect.styles`
- `inspect.custom`
- `defaultOptions`

Only older closed custom-hook behavior issues matched `inspect.custom`; I did not find an open tracker or active PR for the static property surface.

## Acceptance

- `util.inspect.custom` and destructured/captured `inspect.custom` equal `Symbol.for("nodejs.util.inspect.custom")` at runtime.
- `util.inspect.defaultOptions` exists with Node-compatible defaults for the supported inspect option set, and mutating supported defaults affects later `inspect()` calls where Node does.
- `util.inspect.styles` and `util.inspect.colors` expose Node-compatible object/table shape for the supported style names and ANSI color tuples.
- Existing custom-inspect hook fixtures keep passing.

## Summary

Callback-style fd helpers should report bad descriptor and flush/mode failures through the callback error argument. Node calls the callback with an `Error` for invalid fds in `fs.close`, `fs.fsync`, `fs.fdatasync`, and `fs.fchmod`; Perry's callback wrappers currently route through sync helpers/status results and then call the success callback path, or can throw before invoking the callback.

## Node Behavior

Local Node v25.9.0 probe:

```js
const fs = require("node:fs");

for (const [label, call] of [
  ["close", cb => fs.close(987654321, cb)],
  ["fsync", cb => fs.fsync(987654321, cb)],
  ["fdatasync", cb => fs.fdatasync(987654321, cb)],
  ["fchmod", cb => fs.fchmod(987654321, 0o600, cb)],
]) {
  call((err) => console.log(label, err && err.code, err && err.syscall));
}
```

Observed output:

```text
close EBADF close
fsync EBADF fsync
fdatasync EBADF fdatasync
fchmod EBADF fchmod
```

The sync forms throw EBADF, but the callback forms do not throw synchronously for this bad-fd case; they deliver the filesystem error to the callback.

## Perry Behavior

Current source routes these callback forms through sync/status helpers and then calls the success callback path:

- `crates/perry-runtime/src/fs/callbacks.rs::js_fs_close_callback()` calls `js_fs_close_sync(fd)` and then `call_cb0(...)`.
- `js_fs_fsync_callback()` calls `js_fs_fsync_sync(fd)` and then `call_cb0(...)`.
- `js_fs_fdatasync_callback()` calls `js_fs_fdatasync_sync(fd)` and then `call_cb0(...)`.
- `js_fs_fchmod_callback()` calls `js_fs_fchmod_sync(fd, mode)` and then `call_cb0(...)`.

The sync helpers validate fds or return status values:

- `crates/perry-runtime/src/fs/fd_ops.rs::js_fs_close_sync()` validates the fd with syscall name `close`.
- `crates/perry-runtime/src/fs/mod.rs::js_fs_fsync_sync()` and `js_fs_fdatasync_sync()` validate with `fsync` / `fdatasync`.
- `js_fs_fchmod_sync()` validates with `fchmod`, then returns only `1` / `0` for the underlying permission update.

So callback APIs do not have a Node-compatible first-argument error path for invalid descriptors or later syscall failures.

## Suggested PR Cut

Batch this with related issues in:
`node:fs: filesystem error propagation parity cut` (#3248)

Good batch candidates:
- #2749
- #2746
- #2748
- #2752

Do not batch with:
- watcher/glob/stream object behavior (#3249)
- broad argument-validation work outside fs error channels (#2013)
- unrelated `node:fs/promises` manifest exposure

## Acceptance

- parity/regression test proves invalid-fd `fs.close`, `fs.fsync`, `fs.fdatasync`, and `fs.fchmod` callbacks receive `err.code === "EBADF"` with the expected `syscall`
- callback forms do not report success for the same failure cases
- sync forms continue throwing Node-shaped fd errors
- related known-failure/docs/manifest entries updated if touched

## Summary
`new Worker(filename, options)` should honor Node-observable Worker option surfaces such as `stdout`, `stderr`, `stdin`, `env`, `resourceLimits`, `name`, `SHARE_ENV`, and `trackUnmanagedFds`. Perry currently has no Node-compatible Worker constructor, so these stream and option-state rows are untracked outside the broad worker execution issue.

## Node Behavior
A Node v25.9.0 probe shows the stream and option shape:

```js
const { Worker, SHARE_ENV } = require("node:worker_threads");
console.log(typeof SHARE_ENV, String(SHARE_ENV)); // symbol Symbol(nodejs.worker_threads.SHARE_ENV)

const worker = new Worker(`
  const { parentPort } = require("node:worker_threads");
  process.stdout.write("out-line\\n");
  process.stderr.write("err-line\\n");
  parentPort.postMessage({ envProbe: process.env.PERRY_WORKER_ENV_PROBE || null });
`, {
  eval: true,
  stdout: true,
  stderr: true,
  env: { PERRY_WORKER_ENV_PROBE: "child" },
  resourceLimits: { maxOldGenerationSizeMb: 16 },
  name: "stdio-probe",
});

console.log(!!worker.stdout, !!worker.stderr, worker.stdin === null);
```

## Summary
`worker_threads.postMessageToThread(threadId, value[, transferList][, timeout])` should deliver a direct message to another worker thread and surface Node-compatible timeout / same-thread errors. Perry currently has no visible implementation for this module-level direct messaging API.

## Node Behavior
A Node v25.9.0 probe shows the API shape and delivery path:

```js
const { Worker, postMessageToThread, threadId } = require("node:worker_threads");

console.log(typeof postMessageToThread, postMessageToThread.length); // function 4
await postMessageToThread(threadId, { self: true }, undefined, 10);
// rejects with ERR_WORKER_MESSAGING_SAME_THREAD

const worker = new Worker(`
  const { parentPort, threadId } = require("node:worker_threads");
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => {}, 1000);
  process.on("workerMessage", (value, source) => {
    parentPort.postMessage({ got: value, source });
    clearInterval(keepAlive);
  });
  parentPort.postMessage({ ready: true, threadId });
`, { eval: true });
```

Posting to the worker's `threadId` delivers a `process` `workerMessage` event whose `value` is the sent object and whose `source` is the sending thread id. Posting to the same thread rejects with `ERR_WORKER_MESSAGING_SAME_THREAD`; unanswered posts can reject with `ERR_WORKER_MESSAGING_TIMEOUT`.

## Perry Behavior

## Summary
`vm.SourceTextModule` should expose the modern module-request lifecycle helpers used to inspect and instantiate static dependencies: `moduleRequests`, `linkRequests()`, `instantiate()`, `hasTopLevelAwait()`, and `hasAsyncGraph()`. Perry currently has no visible `node:vm` module implementation, and the existing module-linking leaf does not explicitly track this helper surface.

## Node Behavior
A minimal Node v25.9.0 probe under `--experimental-vm-modules` shows the observable helper behavior:

```js
const vm = require("node:vm");
const dep = new vm.SyntheticModule(["default"], function () {
  this.setExport("default", 41);
});
const m = new vm.SourceTextModule('import value from "dep"; export const answer = value + 1;');

console.log(m.status);                                      // "unlinked"
console.log(m.moduleRequests.map(r => [r.specifier, r.phase])); // [["dep", "evaluation"]]
console.log(m.hasTopLevelAwait());                          // false
try { m.hasAsyncGraph(); } catch (err) { console.log(err.code); } // ERR_VM_MODULE_STATUS
m.linkRequests([dep]);
m.instantiate();
console.log(m.status, m.hasAsyncGraph());                   // "linked", false
await m.evaluate();
console.log(m.status, m.namespace.answer);                  // "evaluated", 42
```

## Summary
`node:punycode` has its top-level deprecated conversion surface implemented, but the `punycode.ucs2` helper follow-ups still share one implementation boundary: Node-compatible UTF-16 code-unit handling and invalid-input errors.

This parent groups the remaining `ucs2` work into one medium PR cut instead of separate tiny fixes.

## Child Issues
- #3002 - `node:punycode: preserve surrogate code units in ucs2 helpers`
- #3100 - `node:punycode: preserve ucs2 helper argument errors`

## Intended PR Boundary
Implement `punycode.ucs2.decode()` / `punycode.ucs2.encode()` against JavaScript UTF-16 code units and Node-compatible invalid-input behavior:

- decode should inspect JS UTF-16 code units, combine only valid adjacent surrogate pairs, and preserve lone surrogate code units numerically
- encode should emit strings from Node-compatible code-point inputs, preserve surrogate code units where Node does, and throw for invalid values instead of silently skipping them
- nullish/non-iterable/string/invalid numeric inputs should match Node's observable `TypeError` / `RangeError` behavior
- existing successful astral and BMP round trips should keep passing

## Evidence
- `test-parity/node-suite/punycode/ucs2.ts` covers successful `ucs2` round trips but not lone surrogate or invalid-input behavior.
- `crates/perry-runtime/src/punycode.rs::js_punycode_ucs2_decode()` currently goes through `get_string_content(value)` and `s.chars()`, which cannot expose lone UTF-16 surrogate code units.
- `crates/perry-runtime/src/punycode.rs::js_punycode_ucs2_encode()` currently uses `char::from_u32(v as u32)` and skips values Rust cannot represent as scalar values.
- Local Node v25.9.0 probe confirms Node preserves lone surrogate code units and throws `TypeError` / `RangeError` for invalid inputs.

## Duplicate Search
- `node:punycode ucs2 parity cut`
- `node:punycode UTF-16`
- `punycode ucs2`
- `punycode surrogate`

Found initial closed implementation work #2607 / PR #2626 and the two open follow-up leaves above, but no current parent issue for this PR cut.

## Non-goals
- Do not rework top-level `punycode.encode()` / `decode()` / `toASCII()` / `toUnicode()` behavior in this PR cut.
- Do not handle the email local-part conversion issue #3000 here.
- Do not add broad deprecation-warning or module-loader behavior.

## Acceptance
- child issues #3002 and #3100 have parity/regression coverage and pass
- implementation matches Node observable behavior for lone surrogate code units and invalid `ucs2` inputs
- existing `node:punycode` successful conversion tests continue passing
- related known-failure/docs/manifest entries are updated if touched

## Summary
Group the remaining `node:os` host-derived data mismatches into one medium PR cut. The main `node:os` surface is now much broader than the stale gap docs suggest, but four open leaves still share the same implementation theme: Perry returns shape-compatible values while Node returns host-specific values or applies Node-specific runtime option rules.

This cut should tighten observable host fidelity without reworking already-merged constants, basic platform methods, or import-shape fixes.

## Child Issues

- #3004 - `node:os: honor dynamic buffer encoding in userInfo`
- #3005 - `node:os: match tmpdir environment precedence and trailing slash rules`
- #3006 - `node:os: report real network interface MACs on non-Linux hosts`
- #3007 - `node:os: populate cpus data on macOS instead of fallback zeros`

## Intended PR Boundary

A good implementation PR should cover host-derived `node:os` values that can be proven with deterministic invariants rather than exact machine-specific snapshots:

- runtime option handling for `os.userInfo({ encoding: "buffer" })`, including non-literal option objects
- Node's `os.tmpdir()` environment precedence and trailing-separator normalization
- platform-specific host probes for `os.networkInterfaces()` MAC addresses where available
- platform-specific host probes for `os.cpus()` model/speed/timing data where available

Use invariant-style tests under `test-parity/node-suite/os/**` so the suite stays portable across CI hosts.

## Current Evidence Anchors

- `docs/runtime-parity-gaps.md:366-442` is stale in broad strokes but still shows the historical `node:os` gap surface.
- `test-parity/node-suite/os/**` already has granular tests for `userInfo`, paths, network interfaces, CPUs, constants, imports, and platform methods.
- `crates/perry-runtime/src/os.rs` contains the current host implementations, including `js_os_tmpdir()`, `js_os_user_info()`, `js_os_user_info_buffer()`, `js_os_cpus()`, and `js_os_network_interfaces()`.
- `crates/perry-hir/src/lower/expr_call/globals.rs:785-805` special-cases many `node:os` calls, including static lowering for `userInfo` and native dispatch for priority methods.
- `crates/perry-api-manifest/src/entries.rs:2060-2103` registers the current `node:os` methods/properties, including `version`, priority methods, `EOL`, `devNull`, and `constants`.

## Non-Goals

- Do not redo merged `node:os` work from PRs 1171, 1884, 1887, 1890, 1897, 1909, 1922, or 2618.
- Do not treat the stale 195-gap docs count as authoritative without source/test verification.
- Do not broaden this into every `os.constants` value; constants already have separate merged work and should only be touched if a child issue requires it.
- Do not require exact host values in tests; assert Node-compatible shapes, precedence, nonzero/nonempty invariants, and platform-appropriate behavior.

## Acceptance

- each child issue has a parity/regression test proving the observable mismatch
- implementation matches Node observable behavior for the targeted host-derived data or runtime option rule
- tests avoid brittle machine-specific snapshots
- related known-failure/docs/manifest entries are updated only for surfaces touched by the PR
